World.title: ECZ Validates 40 Nominated MPs As Proportional Representation Enters Parliament
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) has validated 40 nominated Members of Parliament under the new proportional representation system, reserving seats in the National Assembly for women, youths and persons with disabilities for the first time in the country’s history.

The 40 comprise 20 women, 15 youths and five persons with disabilities. They were declared at a validation exercise at the Mulungushi International Conference Centre in Lusaka presided over by ECZ Chairperson Mwangala Zaloumis, who served as Returning Officer. The new members are yet to be sworn in.

Only two parties qualified for the seats, the ruling United Party for National Development (UPND) and the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP). The UPND took 32 of the 40 seats, leaving the NRPUP with eight.

The seats flow from the Constitution of Zambia (Amendment) Act No. 13 of 2025, which provided for additional nominated MPs to guarantee representation for groups that have long struggled to win constituency contests. The Electoral Process (Amendment) Act No. 12 of 2026 set out the mechanics, including the distribution of seats and the submission, processing and publication of party lists.

“This is an important milestone in the implementation of Zambia’s evolving electoral and democratic framework,” Ms Zaloumis said.

She said the constitutional provision was designed to guarantee representation for women, young people and persons with disabilities. “It recognises that a truly representative Parliament must reflect the full diversity of the Zambian population,” she said.

The ECZ chief said every candidate was vetted against the qualifications set out in Articles 70 and 153 of the Constitution before validation. The qualifying parties submitted their finalised lists to the commission once the seats had been allocated, and only the UPND and NRPUP qualified for proportional representation seats in both the National Assembly and local councils.

Ms Zaloumis said the system would allow women to contribute more substantially to national policymaking and give young people a route to bring their perspectives, aspirations and ideas into Parliament. Persons with disabilities, she said, would now take part directly in shaping the laws and policies that affect them.

In the disability category, the UPND secured three seats, filled by Francis Kope, Misheck Mweemba and Lazarus Hakalebula. The NRPUP took two, filled by Mumba Mubanga and Kennedy Phiri.

The youth category went 12 to three. The governing party’s youth nominees are Donald Mwenda, Christine Mwenya, Mukumbuta Mubiyana, Nelia Shikombelo, Michelo Chizombwe, Jemimah Mwaba, Vincent Musilikani, Lloyd Nsonga, Kabaso Mwato, Nsama Mpundu, Gabby Simutowe and Fatima Sichele. The NRPUP named Chanda Chunda, Collins Kampamba and Harris Muntanga.

The UPND secured 17 of the 20 women’s seats. Its nominees include Chama Chileshe, Samwata Manyengu, Chilufya Chikongolo, Grace Sampa, Ireen Muyenga, Getrude Imenda, Kate Nanyangwe, Susan Tembo, Esnart Sakala, Caroline Katotobwe, Judith Kabemba, Melissa Chikwanda, Chonya Mirriam, Mutinta Musokotwane, Mbolongwe Moomba and Catherine Kantumoya. The NRPUP’s three women’s seats went to Julian Kangwa, Mubanga Kapambwe and Susan Peto.

Ms Imenda, the UPND’s deputy secretary general, said the mixed-member system would lift the number of women in the House. She said women had historically been under-represented under the first-past-the-post system, making reserved seats important in broadening representation, and that Zambia, as a signatory to international commitments on gender equality, aims to reach equal representation of women and men by 2030.

Mr Hakalebula, vice-president of the Zambia National Federation of the Blind, described the allocation of five seats for persons with disabilities as a good number and a good starting point. “The voice and needs of people with disabilities will be heard,” he said.

He credited President Hakainde Hichilema with championing the new law, saying the direct inclusion of persons with disabilities in Parliament would amplify their representation in national affairs.

Ms Mwaba, a former vice-president of the University of Zambia Students’ Union (UNZASU) popularly known as Komanda Kwishiba, was picked under the youth category. She said the appointment aligned with the Grow Zambia Agenda, which she described as inclusive, and was joined after her validation by presidential political advisor Levy Ngoma.

“It is a responsibility I take very seriously, and I look forward to contributing to our country’s development while ensuring that the voices of young people are clearly heard,” Ms Mwaba said.

She also addressed students still in school. “I want to encourage other people who are still pursuing their education to remain focused and determined even as they excel in their studies, that they too can advance their dreams one step at a time,” she said.

The two parties that share the new seats led last month’s presidential contest, in which Mr Hichilema secured a second term with 2,965,326 votes against 1,856,217 for NRPUP candidate Brian Mundubile.

The 40 validated members will take their places in the National Assembly once they are sworn in.

World.title: Incoming Cabinet Ministers, Take A Leaf From The Lusaka Mayor!
World.content:
THE new Lusaka Mayor Mwewa Chitambala is like a wounded bull in a China shop. However, the only difference is that, he’s not charging in every direction destroying things, but trying to bring sanity back to the city of Lusaka…… cleaning up the mess that we keep leaving behind!

We are hoping to see a change of mind set very soon and, of course, a much cleaner and welcoming capital city. Can we see all hose shops painted! Can our people stop throwing trash through the windows of cruising vehicles! Can we see street lights worked on! Can we see rubbish bins everywhere! Can we see play parks restored! Can we see buses loading from designated stations!

We firmly believe Mwewa Chitambala hasn’t gone in to mint gold as he was born with a silver spoon in his mouth…….he has gone in to fix things……to clean up the city!

Having laid this groundwork, we now come to the incoming Cabinet Ministers. Why do you expect HH to appoint you as a Cabinet Minister? If your answer is contracts, trips, and enriching yourself, please stay home. President Hichilema does not need passengers, he needs deliverers.

Take a leaf from the Mayor! Do you have any vision for your country or it’s the flag and other appendages attached to the offices which have attracted you?

Some of the Ministers in the previous government were a total let down! They didn’t leave any mark that the nation would remember them for; they were ever sitting in offices drinking tea with cookies or galavanting from one Hotel to another cutting deals. We know them; particularly those from the Copperbelt!

The energy that the new Mayor of city of Lusaka brings to his office is what we expect from Cabinet Ministers! Don’t come to these offices with the mentality of CEOs who should sit in offices the whole day.

If you’re Agriculture Minister, we expect you to take to the field and ensure that farming inputs are being delivered on time. If you’re Energy Minister, we expect you to be industrious and innovative and ensure that investments into alternative energy continue pouring in so that load shedding doesn’t come back. If you’re Local Government Minister, you must make sure CDF isn’t being abused and projects are being completed in good time. If you’re Fisheries Minister we expect you to fill up our rivers with fresh fish stocks. If you’re Small & Medium Enterprises Minister, go to the shanties and empower those youngsters with affordable loans.

Of course the list goes on and on but the most important thing is let’s learn from Chitambala; let’s be passionate about our jobs even if we are aware most of you are going in for the money!

Prince Bill M. Kaping’a

Political/Social Analyst

Zambezi

World.title: A candid evaluation of President Hichilema’s first Cabinet
World.content:
1. Vice-President: W.K. Mutale Nalumango – Even when this arrangement has proven troublesome for most African countries, she has survived the past 5 years and continues into the next term. Mutale can best be described as humble and loyal to the President, eager to implement the bidding of the President at any juncture. In Parliament, she has put her experience to good use, having initially served as Deputy Speaker in the MMD administration, by ably executing her role as Leader of Government Business and even providing motherly advice to truant MPs such as Munir Zulu and Binwell Mpundu.

2. Minister of Finance and National Planning: Situmbeko Musokotwane – Not given to fanfare, he enjoys working quietly in the background. He oversaw the restructuring of roughly $13 billion in external debt after Zambia became the first African country to default during the pandemic. He also secured the IMF Extended Credit Facility and restored macroeconomic stability. Cautious, orthodox, and credible – his retention into the second term is continuity.

3. Minister of Defence: Ambrose Lufuma – Quiet and disciplined. Focused on barracks rehabilitation, welfare of soldiers, and non-partisan military. No major scandals to his name, the country has witnessed the military taking to the field to improve national food security.

4. Minister of Home Affairs and Internal Security: Jack Mwiimbu – The party’s veteran tactician. He managed police reforms, kept relative calm during volatile by-elections, and reduced political cadres at stations. Criticized for slow reform of the Public Order Act and perceptions of selective enforcement. Although he managed to apply the breaks on unnecessary roadblocks and checkpoints, sadly they are now back! It remains to be seen whether he’ll still be maintained in his position.

5. Minister of Justice: Princess Kasune -Mulambo Haimbe (2021-2024) / Princess Kasune (2024-2026) – Haimbe initiated Access to Information Act and constitutional review groundwork. Kasune pushed human rights and gender justice narrative. She’ll be remembered for ensuring the Constitution Amendment Bill No. 7 / 2025 was enacted into law.

6. Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation: Stanley Kakubo (2021-2023) / Mulambo Haimbe (2024-2026) – Kakubo was energetic on economic diplomacy but resigned over a scandal involving bales of cash. Haimbe, a lawyer, brought legal polish and steadied the ministry, pushing for border openness and FDI linkages. It’s hardly surprising that he’s back at Chester House.

7. Minister of Health: Sylvia Masebo (2021-2024) / Elijah Muchima (2024-2026) Alex Katakwe (2026) – Masebo tried to fight drug pilferage and reformed ZAMMSA. Muchima, a former Shushushu took over from her and steadied the ministry, famously warning perennial thieves in the ministry their days were numbered! He was later replaced by Alex Katakwe who shortly committed a faux pas by encouraging thieves in the ministry to steal reasonably. The position has since been awarded to Roma Chilengi.

8. Minister of Education: Douglas Syakalima – Oversaw free education – 2 million children back to school. He managed massive teacher recruitment of 30,000. However, infrastructure lagged – overcrowded classrooms while desk deficits persisted. Student loan schemes were also extended to the other public universities beyond the traditional UNZA and CBU. He was also expected to clean up the ministry by weeding our PF/Tonse aligned officials in his Ministry such as the DEBS and Head Teachers but to no avail.

9. Minister of Energy: Peter Kapala (2021-2024) / Makozo Chikote (2024-2026) – Kapala battled 12-hour load shedding due to the worst drought. When Chikote took over from him, he accelerated putting up of solar power plants. He also spearheaded reforms like tariff blending and net metering. He however faced a backlash for failing to provide 7 hours of power as he had assured the nation after ERB approved an emergency tariff adjustment. President Hichilema publicly told him off. “Don’t announce, let people see the extra hours regarding power supply.” He should’ve handled communication better!

10. Minister of Green Economy and Environment: Collins Nzovu (2021-2024) / Mike Mposha (2024-2026) Mposha ran away from his Munali Constituency once he sensed danger. He didn’t leave much impact worth talking about. The pine forests that KK bequeathed to us are fast depleting while indigenous trees are being harvested willy-nilly and yet we didn’t see any tangible initiatives to replenish the same. Worse still, he failed to champion development of green investments, green jobs, renewable energy let alone energy efficiency

11. Minister of Science and Technology: Felix Mutati – The Silicon Valley in the US is the center for high-tech innovation, computer technology, and the tech industry. It works closely with research universities and is home to big global companies like Apple, Google, and Meta and also a major hub for investors, startups and high profile investments. In Africa, countries like Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa, Egypt and Kenya are already leading the way in replicating their own version of Silicon Valley. Did we see Mutati taking gigantic strides in this direction? Negative! In this era of ICT, we probably need a youngster in this ministry who’s going to easily adapt and move with changing times.

12. Minister of Transport and Logistics: Frank Tayali – those from Ndola would tell you he has changed the face of Ndola! Under his tenure, the country secured a $1.4bn concession with China Civil to rehabilitate the TAZARA while Zambia Airways was relaunched as a national carrier. The provincial airports in Kasama, Chipata, Mongu, Solwezi, Mfuwe, and Mansa were also upgraded. Whatever sins Tayali committed against the people of Ndola for them to send him packing only God knows, perhaps it’s a question of attitude.

13. Minister of Labour and Social Security: Brenda Tambatamba – although she seemed to remain ‘AWOL’ as reports of workers being abused by employers kept surfacing on social media, she was quite instrumental in introducing reforms in her ministry chief among them partial withdrawals, reduced waiting periods for pension payouts and withdrawal of over 4,000 children from child labour. We hope to see her back with much a bigger whip to discipline truant employers!

14. Minister of Lands and Natural Resources: Elijah Muchima (2021-2024) / Sylvia Masebo (2024-2026) – land digitisation and mass titling commenced but is far from over. She also tried to curb deep rooted corruption in the acquisition of land.

15. Minister of Community Development: Doreen Mwamba – although she will be remembered for hosting a National Indaba on Street Kids, the problem of street kids has remained a nightmare.

16. Minister of Agriculture: Reuben R. Phiri Mtolo – although he expanded the Farmer Input Support Programme and reintroduced winter maize, annual maize shortages and high mealie-meal prices continued to haunt him. The drought of 2023/24 exposed over-reliance on rain-fed agriculture.

17. Minister of Fisheries & Livestock: Peter Kapala – he was shuffled from the Ministry of Energy for whatever reasons! Did he do much to decrease the 51, 000 tonnes fish deficit? Well we expected fish-farms being spearheaded all over the country.

18. Minister of Local Government and Rural Development: Gary Nkombo (2021-2025) / Gift Sialubalo (2025-2026) – Face of CDF increase to K30.5m. Empowered the councils although questions on their capacity to manage funds and quality of CDF projects were raised. Sialubalo brought new energy to the ministry, regularly visiting various parts of the country to supervise Councils and addressing teething issues.

19. Minister of Commerce, Trade and Industry: Chipoka Mulenga – Young and market-facing. Pushed SEZs and manufacturing, but trade deficit and influx of cheap imports remained issues for local SMEs. He lamentably failed to lure in meaningful investors let alone coming up with initiatives to ‘birth’ the next generation of Dangotes.

20. Minister of Small & Medium Enterprises: Elias Mubanga – the ministry is expected to be instrumental in inspiring and injecting a new lease of life in small businesses such as bricklaying, welding, mechanics, tailoring and butcheries etc. Did we witness gigantic steps in that direction? Zero!

21. Minister of Information & Media: Chushi Kasanda (2021-2023) / Cornelius Mweetwa (2023-2026) – government communication under Kasanda was quite erratic.Things got better when Mweetwa took over. He proved to be combative and defensive, often clashing with the media.

22. Minister of Mines & Minerals Development: Paul Kabuswe – a Kopala resident, Chililabombwe people expected him to easily understand the challenges of the region and offered practical solutions. Unfortunately, the opposite seemed to be the case! The Black Mountain in Kitwe vanished in thin air without the ordinary people benefitting anything. He equally faced criticism for mishandling other dump sites and artisanal miners.

23. Minister of Tourism: Rodney Sikumba – he was credited with making tourism a serious engine for economic diversification beyond copper! The sector tremendously recovered post-Covid – tourist arrivals more than doubled up, job creation was ramped up while revenue collection remained above target.

24. Minister of Infrastructure, Housing & Urban Development: Charles Milupi – He was in charge of one of the biggest ministries and yet he remained scandal-free. Under his watch, the following roads were upgraded to bituminous standard countrywide: Samfya–Kasaba Road (Luapula Province), Chikankata Road (Southern Province), and Chibuluma Road (Copperbelt), while the Katunda–Lukulu–Watopa–Mumbezhi Road (Western Province) was in the offing and the Ndola–Kitwe Dual Carriageway is well underway. Quiet, technical and loyal – one of the outstanding performers of the first Cabinet.

25. Minister of Youth & Sport: Elvis Nkandu – My former neighbour, aka – Akatuntulu – has proven to be a politician pro-max! Although he was firing on all six cylinders doing what he knows best – party mobilisation – he never neglected his work at the Ministry in any way. Instead of just focusing on football, as his predecessors did in the past, he ensured that other sports disciplines were catered for as well. Our U-17 Girls won the 2025 COSAFA Girls’ Championship and qualified for the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. On the tracks, our athletes hauled over 200 medals across continental and global competitions. He also spearheaded infrastructure rehabilitation and youth empowerment initiatives. This one deserves to be elevated to a much more senior ministry.

26. Minister of Fisheries & Livestock: Peter Kapala – He was appointed on July 29, 2024, after his reassignment from the Ministry of Energy. His focus was livestock exports, aquaculture growth, disease control, and restocking rivers. He repositioned the sector as part of Government’s broader goal to diversify from copper and make agriculture and livestock the pillar of growth. However, the nation expected him to come out with guns blazing after Sino Metals polluted the Kafue River, which resulted in mass fish deaths. His response was measured, technical and legalistic, where the public expected outrage and immediate compensation.

27. Minister of Water Development and Sanitation: Mike Mposha (2021-2024) / Collins Nzovu (2024-2026) – Mposha was the architect: first National Water Strategy, ZIP $5.75bn, Non-Revenue Water Strategy. Nzovu was the builder: Kafulafuta $449m, Nkana II, 12 Small Towns for 1.6m people. Lusaka’s deficit (480k demand vs 185k produced) and Kafue pollution were their albatross. Nzovu faced severe criticism over the manner he handled pollution incidents on the Copperbelt which basically exposed weak WARMA enforcement.

(Minister of Infrastructure, Housing and Urban Development: Charles Milupi* – Alliance partner, engineer. Focused on PPP road projects, but few roads completed within term. Praised for technical depth, criticised for slow pace.)

Prince Bill M. Kaping’a

Political/Social Analyst

Zambezi

World.title: Youth Activist congratulates nominated Youth MPs
World.content:
Youth Activist Michelo Kanchele has congratulated the youths that have been nominated to serve as Members of Parliament (MPs), urging them to work hard and deliver on the expectations of young people and the wider Zambian population.

Mr Kanchele said the nomination of youths to Parliament is a positive step towards enhancing youth participation and representation in national governance.

He said this development demonstrates that the government is walking the talk on its commitment to increasing youth participation in decision-making processes.

Speaking in an interview with the media, Mr Kanchele said he was among the youths who advocated for the acceptance of Bill 7, which he said has now opened up opportunities for greater youth representation in Parliament.

He has since urged the nominated youths to take their responsibilities seriously and use the opportunity to champion issues affecting young people.

Mr Kanchele said the nominated MPs should work diligently, remain accountable to the people and ensure that their contribution to Parliament translates into tangible development.

He also called on the youths to demonstrate that young people can effectively contribute to national development when given an opportunity to serve.

Mr Kanchele further expressed appreciation to the government for what he described as a great initiative aimed at giving young people a greater voice in national affairs.

He said the inclusion of more young people in decision-making is important in ensuring that youth concerns are adequately represented in Parliament and other levels of governance.

World.title: Luangwa Agricultural officers undergo El-Nino effects training
World.content:
An 80-year-old man of Lububa in Luampa District has emerged as a symbol of community-led conservation after securing more than 1,000 hectares of land for forest regeneration.

Mr Mulele Masiye, working closely with traditional leaders has championed the protection of natural resources by converting former farmland into a conservation area.

The initiative has earned praise from government officials, who have described Mr Masiye as a local Green Champion.

Western Province Permanent Secretary Simomo Kapelwa, speaking during a tree-planting event, commended Mr Masiye for his leadership and commitment to environmental protection.

Mr Kapelwa said Mr Masiye’s efforts demonstrated that meaningful environmental action could begin with one committed individual who identifies a need, mobilises others and promotes practical solutions.

He said community-level initiatives were important because local people understood their environment and were best placed to protect it.

Mr Kapelwa encouraged Mr Masiye and other Green Champions to continue working with schools, traditional leaders, government departments, cooperating partners and community groups to expand the initiative.

Provincial Forestry Officer Kanduli Mupeta also called for greater community involvement in forest conservation, particularly the management of existing forests.

Ms Mupeta said indigenous forests were resilient and capable of regenerating when they were not subjected to excessive disturbance.

She said conservation efforts should therefore focus on protecting existing forests, which required relatively less cost and effort compared to restoring heavily degraded areas.

Ms Mupeta further highlighted the role schools could play in conservation, noting that Lububa Primary and Secondary School, with an enrolment of 1,303 learners, provided an opportunity to establish conservation clubs.

She said the clubs could help promote environmental protection among learners and the wider community.

Ms Mupeta also said government, through the Forest Department, had established policies under the Forest Act and Community Forest Regulations to empower communities to manage forests and benefit from them.

She encouraged people living in the area who were passionate about forest conservation to come together and establish community forest management areas.

Ms Mupeta said government could formally recognise such groups under the Forest Act and enter into agreements with them to manage forests according to conditions agreed upon by the communities.

World.title: 14-year-old girl gives birth after alleged defilement
World.content:
A 14-year-old girl in Sinda district, Eastern Province has given birth to a baby boy following a pregnancy which allegedly came as a result of being defiled several times in the bushes of Wada village in Chief Nyanje.

The incident, which allegedly occurred between December 2025 and June 2026, was reported to Sinda Police Station on Thursday, September 17, 2026, at 14:50 hours.

Eastern Province Police Commanding Officer Robertson Mweemba said the victim was allegedly defiled by a man identified only as Adusha, a resident of Chikwendo Village in Chief Nyanje’s area.

Mr Mweemba said the victim’s 52-year-old mother, Mary Zulu, reported the matter on behalf of her daughter, whom police said is believed to have an intellectual disability.

He said the matter came to light after the victim travelled to Rufunsa District in June 2026 to stay with her elder sister, Misozi Sakala Where the victim was noticed with unusual physical changes but denied being pregnant.

World.title: Govt seeks Tech partnerships to build local capacity
World.content:
Government has called for technology partnerships that build local capacity and ensure investments continue to generate value for Zambia beyond the delivery of projects.

Ministry of Technology and Science Permanent Secretary Brilliant Habeenzu said Zambia does not want to merely purchase technology but also develop local capabilities through skills and technology transfer.

Dr Habeenzu said Zambia’s digital sector had recorded significant growth between 2021 and 2025, with mobile subscriptions increasing from about 20.2 million to more than 26 million, while internet subscriptions rose from 10.4 million to 14.68 million.

He said internet penetration increased from 56.7 percent to 72.1 percent during the period, while fibre-optic coverage expanded from about 15,000 kilometres to more than 42,000 kilometres.

Dr Habeenzu, who was represented by Director of Technical Services Bwanga Mbula, said communication towers increased from 3,413 to 3,769, with nearly 600 sites upgraded towards fifth-generation (5G) technology.

He further said mobile-money transactions increased from K169 billion in 2021 to K486 billion in 2024, while the number of registered agents rose from about 134,000 to more than 556,000.

He said the Government’s approach is anchored on economic transformation, private-sector-led growth, job creation for young people and increased participation of Zambian companies in technology value chains.

Dr Habeenzu said the growth of the digital sector demonstrated the importance of strengthening local capacity, adding that more needed to be done to further enhance Zambia’s digital capabilities.

He said technology partnerships should be based on mutual respect and benefit, genuine skills and technology transfer, job creation, local value retention, compliance with Zambian laws, transparency and integrity in contracting, and long-term commitment.

Dr Habeenzu commended Avit Information Technology Limited for creating a platform that enables Zambian enterprises to work alongside international technology companies.

He was speaking when he welcomed a high-level delegation from Hikvision Digital Technology Company Limited, led by its president Xu Peng, and expressed hope that the engagement would result in expanded collaboration, strengthened local capabilities and increased opportunities for young people.

And Hikvision Digital Technology Company Limited, president Xu Peng, said the Company is involved in telecommunications, the manufacture of drones and cameras, as well as the production of equipment for the agricultural and mining sectors.

He said the partnership between Hikvision and Avit had the potential to deliver benefits to both Zambia and China.

Meanwhile, Avit Information Technology Limited Chief Executive Officer Jacob Lubasi said Zambia was well positioned to achieve the transformation envisaged under the 2026-2032 development agenda through increased adoption of digital technology.

Mr Lubasi said the partnership between Avit and Hikvision would combine licensed local capabilities with advanced technology to provide solutions tailored to Zambia’s national priorities.

He said protecting infrastructure was important not only for the financial sustainability of institutions but also for national security, economic development and effective service delivery.

Mr Lubasi said digital evolution, artificial intelligence, photonic digital technology, automated sensing and cloud-edge computing would play an important role in Zambia’s development.z

According to Mr Onanuga, the dinner reflected the longstanding relationship between Nigeria and France.

President Bola Tinubu met French President Emmanuel Macron on Thursday for a private dinner at the Élysée Palace in Paris.

It is the latest in the series of meetings and engagements between Nigeria and France since Mr Tinubu assumed office in 2023.

The president's Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, disclosed the meeting in a post on X on Friday. He also shared photographs of the two leaders at the French presidential palace.



PREMIUM TIMES reports that the meeting took place while Mr Tinubu was in France during the second leg of his three-week annual leave in Europe.

He arrived in Paris on Monday after spending the first part of his leave in London.

According to Mr Onanuga, the dinner reflected the longstanding relationship between Nigeria and France.

In the post, he wrote, "French President Emmanuel Macron received President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for a private dinner Thursday night at the Élysée Palace, reflecting the enduring relationship between Nigeria and France and their shared commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation."

President Tinubu, in a separate post about the meeting, also said his conversation with Mr Macron reflects both countries' mutual interest in maintaining good relations and strengthening the existing partnership.

He also thanked the French president for his hospitality and friendship.

"It was a pleasure to share a private dinner with President Emmanuel Macron at the Élysée Palace in Paris. @EmmanuelMacron

"Our conversation reaffirmed the strong friendship between Nigeria and France, as well as our shared commitment to deepening cooperation and building a mutually beneficial partnership between our two nations," he wrote.

Photographs released from the dinner showed Mr Tinubu and Mr Macron together at the Élysée Palace, with another image showing Mr Tinubu, Mr Macron and France's First Lady, Brigitte Macron.

However, details of the interaction or any potential agreement between the two leaders were not provided.

World.title: Guinea: Guinea Bans France 24, Withdraws Jeune Afrique Correspondent's Accreditation
World.content:
Dakar — The Committee to Protect Journalists calls on Guinean authorities to reverse Thursday's ban on France 24 after a presenter called President Mamadi Doumbouya a "putschist president" and to reinstate the accreditation of the pan-African weekly Jeune Afrique's Guinea correspondent Diawo Barry.

"By prohibiting France 24 from broadcasting and Jeune Afrique's Diawo Barry from working, Guinean authorities have shown their ruthless determination to silence independent voices and to intimidate other media outlets into self-censorship," said Moussa Ngom, CPJ's Francophone Africa representative. "Authorities must immediately reverse these decisions and refrain from further actions that erode press freedom and the public's right to information."

In its September 17 decision, the regulatory High Authority of Communication (HAC) said it had banned France 24 because it had failed to comply with its order the previous day "to immediately cease using terms deemed derogatory to the dignity of the Head of State and to make the required editorial corrections." The HAC also withdrew press accreditation for all the French state-owned channel's correspondents, special correspondents, and contributors in Guinea.

On Monday, a France 24 presenter used the word "putschist" while commenting on Doumbouya's visit to Ivory Coast.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Hours after the HAC's September 16 notice, France 24 added an online correction to the video's description, saying that Doumbouya had been "mistakenly labeled a coup leader."

"Having seized power in a coup on September 5, 2021, which overthrew President Alpha Condé, he was subsequently elected President of the Republic following the presidential election of December 28, 2025," the correction said.

France 24 told Agence France-Presse news agency that it had also apologized and corrected the error on air.

Also on September 16, the HAC revoked Barry's accreditation as Jeune Afrique's correspondent on the grounds that his coverage of news in Guinea did not meet the requirements of objective, neutral, balanced reporting.

The Guinean satirical newspaper Le Lynx, where Barry is publishing director, suggested that Jeune Afrique's September special report on Guinea, "Democracy under surveillance," had "ruffled feathers."

Jeune Afrique said that the HAC's decision had been handed down "without prior consultation" and was "not based on any specific allegation" to support its "vague" accusations.

Since Doumbouya took power, the HAC has introduced long-term and indefinite bans on numerous critical outlets and reporters. The whereabouts of journalist Habib Marouane Camara, who was seized by uniformed men in 2024, and of exiled journalist Mamoudou Babila Keita's elderly father, Elhadj Adama Keita, who was kidnapped in 2025, remain unknown.

Close 

CPJ's calls to request comment from the HAC went unanswered.

World.title: Nigeria: Niger State Imposes 24-Hour Curfew After Suspects Die in Custody
World.content:
The Niger State Government has imposed a 24-hour curfew across Minna, the state capital, as tension rises over the deaths of about 37 suspected illegal miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC).

The curfew takes effect immediately after Juma'at prayers on Friday, the government announced.

The government has also ordered the suspension of all mining activities in the state until further notice.

The directives are part of the state government's measures to address the prevailing security situation and restore safety across the state.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The government advised residents to remain indoors and comply fully with the curfew and other security directives until further notice.

The government also cancelled an All Progressives Congress (APC) rally scheduled for Minna on Saturday and suspended the NSCDC State Commandant, Suberu Aniviye, and his team.

Governor Mohammed Bago announced the measures during a press briefing in Minna on Friday.

He said the curfew was necessary to prevent a breakdown of law and order and to allow the government to manage the situation while investigations continue.

Background to the curfew

The deaths occurred after the NSCDC detained suspects arrested in connection with mining activities in the Ema Ushishi area of Niger State.

More than 37 detainees reportedly died while in custody, although the exact number and cause of the deaths have not been officially established.

The bodies were later moved to a mortuary, a development that heightened tension among youths and residents in Minna.

The incident triggered public concern and fears of possible protests or violence, prompting the state government to cancel the APC rally and impose the curfew.

Mr Bago described the deaths as tragic and unacceptable and said the government had begun steps to establish what happened.

He announced the constitution of a committee of inquiry to investigate the incident and determine the cause of the deaths.

Cause of death not established

The governor cautioned against concluding the forensic examinations, medical assessments, and autopsies.

He said possible causes being considered included suffocation caused by overcrowding in the detention facility and exposure to hazardous substances allegedly linked to illegal mining.

"There is no official root cause of these deaths yet. It is too early for anybody to conclude the root causes," Mr Bago said.

He said the state government was compiling a register of the deceased to identify and contact their families.

Mr Bago assured the victims' relatives that the government would engage with them and provide the necessary support during the investigation.

NSCDC commandant suspended

The governor announced the immediate suspension of Mr Aniviye and his team to allow for an impartial investigation.

He said the suspension was not a declaration of guilt but a measure to ensure that the investigation was conducted without interference.

The governor said the Director-General of the NSCDC, who is currently outside the country, had delegated his deputy to represent him in engagements concerning the incident.

He added that the state government had already met with the senior NSCDC official.

'We will probe deeply'

Mr Bago pledged that the government would investigate the incident thoroughly and ensure that those responsible for any wrongdoing were held accountable.

"Lives of human beings are lives of human beings. Such an unjust government will not tolerate any injustice, and we are going to make sure that we probe this thing deeply until we get to the root of this," he said.

He urged residents, particularly youths, to remain calm and obey the curfew.

Close 

"We are calling on all the youth to please stay away from violence. It is not going to bring about those who have died. It will rather cost us a lot at the end of the day," he said.

Mining suspended

The governor also ordered the closure of activities at the illegal mining site in Ema Ushishi.

He expressed concern over mining operations conducted without adequate technology, safety equipment and protective gear.

According to him, such practices expose miners to dangerous conditions and may have contributed to the incident.

The state government said it would continue to work with the NSCDC, the police, the State Security Service and other relevant agencies to establish the facts.

Mr Bago commiserated with the families of the deceased and declared three days of mourning in the state.

He said the cancellation of the APC rally was intended to allow the state to mourn the victims and focus on restoring calm and completing the investigation.

World.title: Sorority alumnae take legal fight to federal court after being 'given a brother' instead of sisterhood
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Sorority alumnae returned to federal court Monday, asking judges to revive their lawsuit against Kappa Kappa Gamma after they alleged the sorority's national leadership improperly allowed a chapter to admit a transgender woman.

Plaintiff Allie Coghan told Fox News Digital that while she has since graduated, she hopes the appeal will establish a clear legal precedent that protects single-sex private spaces and keeps national organizations from overriding local member consent.

"We were promised a sisterhood, and we were given a brother," Coghan said. "If Kappa wants to redefine the word woman to include men in the definition, that's fine, but they have to go through the proper procedures to do so and allow members to vote, which they did not."

SMITH COLLEGE 'MAKES A MOCKERY' OF ALL-WOMEN STATUS BY ADMITTING TRANSGENDER STUDENTS, EDUCATION WATCHDOG SAYS

The legal fight stems from 2022, when transgender student Artemis Langford was allowed to join the University of Wyoming chapter of Kappa Kappa Gamma. Coghan said despite reservations from her and other sorority sisters, Langford was admitted into the sorority.

Coghan said the chapter did not follow its normal voting procedures during the process. Instead of using what she described as the chapter’s traditional recruitment app, Coghan said members were required to submit non-anonymous Google Forms attached to their email addresses.

"They were knocking on girls' doors asking for proof that you had voted," Coghan said, adding that officers told members they would be labeled "transphobic" if they voted against membership.

Coghan said that, despite attempts by members and parents to contact the organization’s national leadership, executives did not answer phone calls and eventually stopped answering emails. She and several of her sorority sisters ultimately launched a legal challenge.

US OLYMPIAN'S LAWSUIT AGAINST USA FENCING FOR ALLEGED TRANS ATHLETE IN WOMEN'S COMPETITION IS DISMISSED

The initial lawsuit was dismissed by U.S. District Judge Alan B. Johnson, who ruled that Kappa Kappa Gamma, as a private organization, could interpret its own membership requirements. However, the alumnae, supported by the Independent Women's Law Center, appealed the ruling to the 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, which heard oral arguments in Denver Monday.

"It was very surreal to be back. I mean, we were in college. We just wanted to be sorority girls, finish our degrees, graduate, go out into the real world," Coghan said.

"I remember when I was trying to decide if I wanted to sign my name on this, asking the lawyer, am I [going to] be married with kids before there's any sort of resolution? And he just kind of laughed at me and said, ‘I guess it depends on how soon you get married.’ Well, I actually just got married two weeks ago," she added.

FEMALE VIRGINIA OFFICER SUES POLICE DEPARTMENT AFTER ALLEGEDLY SHARING LOCKER ROOM WITH BIOLOGICAL MALE

Coghan described the situation in school as toxic and said the sorority house became a "political war zone." She said that while Langford did not live in the house, the student was granted 24/7 access to the living quarters and common rooms, including an area young women needed to walk through to get to the showers.

"The entire dynamic of the house completely shifted. It became a political war zone," Coghan said. "You would see him sitting in the common rooms upstairs, and girls have to walk past those rooms to get to the shower. We don’t have a space to undress to get into the shower, so you would just walk in your towel and go take a shower and come back."

While Coghan has since graduated, she said a sense of duty to younger women keeps her involved in the case and seeking a resolution in the courts.

"I don't understand how the feminist movement has shifted so much that it's no longer pro-women, it's pro-woman erasure," Coghan said.

"I hope that it will really set a standard of woman means woman. Woman does not mean man who thinks he is woman. Woman is not up for interpretation. A woman is an adult human female," she later added.

Coghan and her fellow plaintiff, Hannah Holtmeier, also spoke on the "Riley Gaines Show" podcast, discussing the moment they said their chapter president told them that if they didn’t like the change in their house, they were welcome to drop out of the group.

"She basically told us, 'If you don't like it, your values don't align with Kappa's, and you can drop,'" Holtmeier told Gaines. "Being told that, 'If you don't like it, you can drop' and not live in a house that I had called a home for already a year and a half was absolutely mind-boggling to me."

NHS DOCTOR SUES AFTER 'BEARDED' TRANS PATIENT ALLEGEDLY EXPOSES HIMSELF ON WOMEN'S PSYCHIATRIC WARD

She echoed Coghan’s comments about conditions in the sorority house, saying women would sometimes act as lookouts for one another when they were in the shower to ensure the hallway was clear.

"It was to the point where girls would have like a lookout basically when they're in the shower. They would text their roommate, say, ‘Hey, I'm coming back,’ and they would have to clear the hall," Holtmeier said.

"It was definitely an unnerving feeling in those intimate spaces, especially upstairs when that's where our showers were."

The recent oral arguments before the 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in Denver represented a new phase in the legal battle. The three-judge panel is considering whether to overturn the lower court’s dismissal and revive the breach of contract lawsuit.

The plaintiffs argued the national leadership of the group could not legally redefine core membership terms, including what constitutes being a "woman," without a formal vote from the organization's members or an amendment to its bylaws. The appeals court’s ruling will determine whether the lawsuit remains dismissed or is allowed to move forward.

World.title: Why the House let out early is a matter of debate after Johnson says chamber has 'done its work'
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

It’s a matter of debate as to why House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., sent the House home a day early this week. This is in addition to the House lopping off two additional weeks from its schedule later this month and into early October.

"We're going to modify the House schedule by a day. And let me explain to you why. The House has done its work," Johnson said as House members fled Capitol Hill early Wednesday night. "House Republicans are going now back to our districts. We're going to make the case to the American people on what we have delivered on their behalf."

The House isn’t scheduled to reconvene until Nov. 9, just after the midterms.

But outgoing Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., believes there’s a different reason Johnson cut everyone loose early. The Kentucky Republican introduced eight articles of impeachment for Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth. Because Massie’s push for impeachment is "privileged," the House had 48 hours max to consider the articles.

THE HITCHHIKER’S GUIDE TO MASSIE SAYING JOHNSON IS SENDING THE HOUSE HOME EARLY TO PREVENT HEGSETH IMPEACHMENT

"I figured out why we canceled tomorrow," Massie said. "Tomorrow would be the vote on impeaching Secretary of Defense Peter Bryan Hegseth. And it looks like that vote's not going to happen."

A senior House Republican leadership source insisted to Fox last week that members would be on Capitol Hill "for a full week."

But, by Wednesday, the House had synced up with the Senate and passed the Russia sanctions bill. It OK'd legislation to protect consumers from high electricity and water bills associated with data centers, foisting the cost on tech companies. Yes, there were calls by bipartisan lawmakers that the House should remain in session to address intensifying concerns about AI. But the House was running out of floor traffic.

Except for Massie’s measure to impeach Hegseth.

REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: HOUSE CONTROL COULD HINGE ON WHETHER THE OLD POLITICAL RULES STILL APPLY

Now you can determine for yourself why Johnson dismissed lawmakers a day early — to say nothing of the plan for the House to cut town two weeks sooner than originally planned.

But you can imagine what Massie thought.

"Exactly what I predicted," Massie said on the House floor. "Why did he just cut another day off the calendar?"

I found Massie off the floor after he concluded his speech.

"Do you think they adjourned the House because you have the votes on Hegseth?" yours truly asked.

"Chad, they cut two weeks off of the calendar to keep me from getting to 218 votes on the Epstein discharge petition. And then we came into this week, and I introduced eight articles of impeachment against Peter Hegseth, and they have 48 hours to vote on that," Massie replied.

"He cut off the day tomorrow to avoid the vote."

Here are the parliamentary mechanics.

The House was compelled to consider Massie’s impeachment articles if it met this past Thursday. Otherwise, the resolution covering the eight impeachment articles would expire. The 48-hour window associated with such privileged resolutions disappears. Sure. Massie could bring them up when the House next meets in November. But that is seven weeks from now.

But let’s say the House met on Thursday and was forced to bring up Massie’s impeachment articles. Republicans would likely have offered "a motion to table." This is an effort to kill Massie’s gambit. Thus, the vote would not have been on impeaching Hegseth, but whether or not to set aside Massie’s plan.

If the House voted to table Massie’s articles of impeachment, the gig is up. It’s done. The House never even considered the actual impeachment resolutions. The vote was one step removed from a straight, up/down vote on actually impeaching Hegseth.

But let’s say the motion to table was to fail? That means the House immediately skips to the articles of impeachment. The possibility suddenly exists that Hegseth could face eight impeachment votes even through there’s been no investigation. No committee hearings. No "process."

Nowhere does it say in the Constitution that Congress is required to wrestle with the usual parliamentary volutions to impeach someone. If a simple majority in the House votes to impeach you, you’re impeached.

Nuff said.

REPORTER’S NOTEBOOK: CONGRESS MEETS AI AS FEARS OF HUMAN EXTINCTION JOLT CAPITOL HILL

This is why Republicans likely would have moved to table Massie’s impeachment articles. A vote to table inoculates members from having to take a challenging vote on the underlying issue. Keep in mind that there are a number of House Republicans who are aggravated with Hegseth and beside themselves about the war in Iran. This vote would have put them in an interesting position, especially since many if not all Democrats may have voted to impeach.

So, I asked Massie the following about the motion to table.

"That would have put (members) in a tough spot. Or, if they had to vote on that, would it have passed?" I asked.

"A vote on a motion to table? He may not have survived that vote," Massie declared.

In other words, Massie believes the House could have defeated the motion to table. That would have triggered votes on actually impeaching Hegseth. And, from Massie’s standpoint, that’s why Johnson sent the House home.

You might remember that there was a bipartisan effort last summer by Massie and Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., to go around Johnson and deposit a measure on the floor, forcing release of the Epstein files. Johnson let the House out early for summer break then. Later, Johnson kept the House out of session for most of the 43-day government shutdown as the special effort to bring action on the resolution loomed.

The House voted to reopen the government in mid-November. And one of the first things the House did after that? Voted 427-1 to require a release of the files. The lone nay vote against releasing the files? Rep. Clay Higgins, R-La.

Even though there aren’t votes until early November, Massie is still a member of the House. He’ll be a member in the lame duck session through early January. Massie lost his primary to Republican Ed Gallrein, a candidate backed by President Donald Trump.

And Hegseth took the unusual step of traveling to northern Kentucky this spring to campaign for Gallrein.

World.title: Paramount appears to learn from its 'Big Brother' racial double standard on 'The Challenge'
World.content:
Three contestants were abruptly removed from MTV’s long-running athletic reality competition series "The Challenge" this week following a reported racial incident that the show chose not to air.

At the beginning of Wednesday’s episode of "The Challenge: Cutthroat," host T.J. Lavin entered the house without Leo Dionicio, Josh Goldstein and Nelson Thomas present.

"Leo, Nelson and Josh all broke the code of conduct here on 'The Challenge,' so they're all gone," Lavin told the remaining contestants.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The show did not air the incident that led to the three disqualifications or provide any additional details.

Page Six reported that Dionicio, who is Black, used the N-word during a game and Goldstein, who is White, repeated it. According to the report, Thomas became angry over Goldstein’s use of the word and later damaged the kitchen. Production then removed all three contestants.

The Paramount+ original is the 42nd season of the long-running MTV franchise. "The Challenge" is generally classified as reality television, but the modern version is built around athletic competition. Contestants run, swim, climb, wrestle, carry heavy weight and race through obstacle courses that test strength, endurance and mental toughness. Seasons typically end with a grueling final that can stretch across multiple days and resemble an adventure race more than a reality show.

The controversy also bears a striking resemblance to one Paramount faced three years ago on another reality competition show. The company appears to have learned from a racial double standard it applied back then.

Nelson Thomas and Leo Dionicio address 'The Challenge' disqualifications

Thomas subsequently confirmed at least part of the reported account.

"I let my emotions take over, broke dishes, destroyed [the] kitchen and violated the code of conduct," Thomas wrote on X. "That’s on me."

Thomas also claimed that Goldstein apologized to him privately and urged Goldstein to address the situation publicly.

"Saying you have Black friends doesn’t give you a pass to use the N-word," Thomas wrote.

Dionicio, meanwhile, discussed his removal during an appearance on fellow "Challenge" competitor Johnny "Bananas" Devenanzio’s "Death, Taxes and Bananas" podcast.



At the beginning of the discussion, Devenanzio said they had been instructed "from the top" not to reveal the specifics of the incident. Despite that, Dionicio argued that he did not deserve to be included in the mass disqualification.

"I was really, really upset because what was said was super ignorant," Dionicio said. "I thought the hand I was dealt was pretty messed up considering I didn’t really do s--- wrong."

Dionicio said he believed one contestant should have been fined, another should have been removed and he should not have been punished at all.

Johnny "Bananas" pushed back on Dionicio’s argument.

"I think what’s understood is that they have to have a rule, and it has to apply to everybody equally," he said.

Later in the conversation, however, Dionicio acknowledged that every contestant had signed the same agreement.

"I know we all signed the same contract," Dionicio said. "It’s just frustrating because I didn’t really think that would apply to me. But then I realized, you know, I’m not bigger than the program, unfortunately."

Dionicio never explicitly said, "I’m Black, so I should be allowed to use the N-word." But taken together, his comments strongly suggest that is his position. He reportedly used the word, said he did not believe the rule should have applied to him and then emphasized in a separate post on X that he is Black and Afro-Latino.

Paramount declined to discuss the specific actions that led to each contestant’s removal. A source familiar with the production said Bunim/Murray Productions has a clear code of conduct and that all three cast members were removed after violating it. The source directed OutKick to Thomas’ public comments about the incident.

The response did not confirm whether Dionicio and Goldstein were removed for using the same word or whether the same provision was applied to both contestants. But Paramount also did not dispute the reported account or challenge OutKick’s interpretation that the rule was enforced equally. Dionicio and Goldstein did not respond to requests for comment prior to publication.

Paramount faced a similar controversy on "Big Brother" in 2023

In August 2023, CBS removed "Big Brother" contestant Luke Valentine after he used the N-word inside the house. The network said Valentine violated the show’s code of conduct and that it had "zero tolerance" for the use of a racial slur.

Except, as OutKick reported at the time, another contestant, Kirsten Elwin, had used the same word days earlier and received no apparent punishment.

Valentine is White. Elwin is Black.

At the time, I wrote that CBS could not claim to have a zero-tolerance rule while applying different consequences based on the race of the person who violated it.

I wasn’t arguing that a White person and a Black person using the N-word carry the same social meaning because they don’t.

But a television production’s code of conduct is either a rule or it isn’t. If contestants are told that a particular word is prohibited, their skin color should not determine whether the rule applies to them.

CBS and MTV were both under the Paramount umbrella when the "Big Brother" incident occurred, just as they are now. This time, the company appears to have applied the standard equally.

Again, Paramount’s refusal to explain the disqualifications prevents us from saying that definitively. But the available reporting indicates that Dionicio and Goldstein used the same word and were both removed from the competition. Dionicio’s subsequent comments suggest he believed being Black should have changed how the rule applied to him.

If the reported account is accurate, production enforced the rule against everyone rather than determining who was socially entitled to violate its conduct policy.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Paramount deserves credit for apparently correcting the double standard it applied on "Big Brother" in 2023. Now it should be transparent enough to confirm that equal enforcement is exactly what happened.

World.title: Google says its AI model gained unauthorized access to three outside systems
World.content:
Google on Friday disclosed the first known instance of its artificial intelligence software, Gemini, carrying out an undirected computer hack, weeks after similar disclosures by AI firms Anthropic and OpenAI raised security alarms about AI models going beyond the instructions of their human creators.

Google said in a statement that in May its AI model gained unauthorized access to three outside systems during a test by either guessing login information or using login credentials it found in a public repository.

Heather Adkins, a Google vice president for security engineering, said in the statement that the AI model thought that the outside computer systems “were part of the test,” but she said in all three instances, the model stopped before doing anything further with its access.

00:00 00:00 How exactly could AI cause widespread danger? 02:35

“In a standard evaluation, the model found public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test,” she said.

Google said it did not consider the unauthorized logins to rise to the level of misalignment, the AI industry term for software going rogue or not following instructions. Instead, the company said the intrusions resulted from mistaken identity, where Gemini thought it was operating within a test but was actually connected to the real internet. Google said the model corrected itself and the company believed the intrusions did not cause any damage.

“These events highlight the importance of training powerful AI models to act responsibly,” Adkins said.

Fears about AI agents going rogue have spiked in recent months since OpenAI said in July that one of its agents had hacked an AI startup, Hugging Face. OpenAI has continued to disclose what it calls examples of other “unexpected or concerning” behavior by AI agents, and Anthropic has described similar behavior by its AI software, Claude.

The OpenAI headquarters in San Francisco. Fears about AI agents going rogue have spiked in recent months. David Paul Morris / Bloomberg via Getty Images

Sydney Von Arx, CEO of Nightingale Collective, an organization focused on AI safety, questioned why Google did not disclose the intrusions sooner.

“At this point I think it’s clear we cannot expect companies to voluntarily come forward and publicly disclose when their agents go rogue, escape, and hack companies,” she said.

She also said she believed Google was too hasty to say that the incidents don’t rise to the level of misalignment. “That’s exactly what Anthropic said after their incidents,” she said.

Anthropic later said its “preliminary analysis was constrained due to our desire to disclose incidents in a timely manner.”

Google said the company did not learn about the intrusions until July, when Irregular, an AI-focused cybersecurity company that was carrying out the tests on Gemini when the intrusions occurred, reviewed its work to look for incidents similar to the Hugging Face disclosure.

Google said it then investigated, informed the organizations behind the websites of the intrusions and told federal authorities about the hacks.

Irregular said it did not believe the incident to be a “sophisticated cyber action” and “there are no current open issues.” It said it planned to release a paper in a few weeks “to share best practices for containment and securely running cyber evals.”

The intrusions were reported earlier Friday by The Wall Street Journal.

AI safety concerns have now reached a fever pitch, with a handful of AI researchers resigning from their jobs and a diverse array of people calling for coordinated action to protect the security of vital systems. Those calls, though, have met with skepticism from the White House and in the Chinese government.

World.title: The first mRNA flu shot is now available. Here’s who can get it.
World.content:
The first mRNA flu shot is now available, but not everyone is eligible.

Moderna’s mFlusiva is the first flu vaccine in the United States to use messenger RNA technology, the same platform used in Pfizer and Moderna’s Covid shots. Scientists have long been interested in using mRNA against the flu because the vaccines can be made faster, potentially making it easier to keep up with changing flu strains.

It’s too early to predict how severe the upcoming flu season will be and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention hasn’t started tracking cases yet. The CDC recommends getting vaccinated by the end of October.

In a late-stage clinical trial, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in May, mFlusiva was found to be about 27% more effective than a standard flu shot. The Food and Drug Administration approved mFlusiva in August for people 50 and older, clearing the way for the shot to reach pharmacies in time for this year’s flu season.

Pharmacies, however, say the new vaccine is already causing confusion among some patients about who can get it, how it compares with traditional flu shots and where people will be able to find it.

Here’s what you need to know:

Who can get the new mRNA flu shot?

The mRNA vaccine is available only for people 50 and older.

“If you have not celebrated your 50th birthday, this vaccine should be of no interest to you,” said Emlah Tubuo, an independent pharmacist in Ohio.

The FDA granted traditional approval for adults 50 to 64 and accelerated approval for people 65 and older, with Moderna required to conduct another trial in that age group. People who do not want the mRNA vaccine can still get a traditional flu shot.

The additional trial in adults 65 and older stems from a controversy that nearly derailed the vaccine’s approval.

In a large clinical trial, Moderna compared mFlusiva with a standard-dose flu shot in people 65 and older, even though the CDC recommends a high-dose flu shot for that age group.

The FDA initially refused to review Moderna’s application over that issue before reversing course and agreeing to a post-approval clinical trial. In June, the FDA’s independent vaccine advisory panel unanimously recommended the approval of the vaccine for older adults.

People younger than 50 won’t be able to get mFlusiva this flu season. Instead, they can get one of the other flu vaccines approved for their age group.

How is the mRNA shot different from a traditional flu shot?

The biggest difference is how the vaccines teach the immune system to recognize influenza.

Most traditional flu shots use a deactivated version of the virus — often grown in eggs — to teach the immune system how to fight it.

MFlusiva uses a small snippet of genetic code to train the body to recognize and fight the flu virus. The mRNA from the vaccine is then broken down and does not remain in the body.

“It’s like a temporary instruction to your immune system to alert your body’s natural defense to recognize influenza,” Tubuo said. It takes about two weeks after vaccination to build protection.

One point of confusion among patients, according to Brigid Groves, a pharmacist with the American Pharmacists Association, is whether mFlusiva also protects against Covid. It doesn’t. The vaccine only targets the flu and is separate from Moderna’s combination Covid and flu vaccine, which was approved by the European Union in April.

Like the traditional seasonal flu vaccines this year, Moderna’s shot is a trivalent vaccine, targeting two influenza A strains and one influenza B strain.

Another difference is that Moderna’s vaccine can be made faster, said Dr. William Schaffner, an infectious disease specialist at Vanderbilt University Medical Center.

Scientists typically have to choose which flu strains to target months before flu season begins, leaving time to manufacture millions of doses. Traditional flu vaccines can take about six months to produce, while Moderna says mFlusiva can be made in two to three months. That shorter timeline, Schaffner said, allows them to wait longer before choosing which strains to target, giving them a better idea of which ones are likely to circulate.

Is the mRNA shot safe and effective?

Published data from a Phase 3 clinical trial suggests mFlusiva should work better than a standard-dose flu shot.More than 40,000 adults 50 and older across 11 countries, including the United States, participated in the trial. The trial found mFlusiva was about 27% more effective than the standard-dose vaccine at preventing laboratory-confirmed illness.

FDA reviewers did not identify any serious safety problems with the vaccine.

Rates of side effects — such as injection-site pain, fatigue and headaches — were more common in the mFlusiva group but still mild to moderate.

Schaffner said the higher rate of side effects may be “a reflection of the vigor with which the immune system responds to the vaccine.”

Will insurance cover mFlusiva?

MFlusiva is reaching pharmacies without a formal recommendation from the CDC or its vaccine advisory committee, a step typically needed to require insurers to cover vaccines for free.

A spokesperson for AHIP, a trade group for health insurers, said it expects most private insurers will cover the vaccine.

Dorit Reiss, a vaccine policy expert at University of California Law San Francisco, said Medicare is required to fully cover the cost of FDA-approved seasonal flu shots.

Reiss said it remains unclear, however, how widely Medicaid will cover the new shot this season, as the program typically requires a formal recommendation from the CDC’s vaccine advisory committee.

According to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, mFlusiva has a price tag of around $171 per dose without insurance. Depending on the pharmacy, the cost could be as low as $154, according to GoodRx.

Where can people get it?

As with any vaccines, whether you can get the shot right away will depend on your local pharmacy’s current stock and delivery schedule.

In a statement, a Moderna spokesperson said the company has begun shipping doses of mFlusiva across the U.S.

Amy Thibault, a CVS Health spokesperson, said mFlusiva is available at its U.S. pharmacies. A Walgreens spokesperson said it expects to begin receiving shipments of the vaccine any day now, although it’ll be available to patients in “limited quantities” this season.

Tubuo, the Ohio pharmacist, said that demand for mFlusiva is currently low, noting that it is still early in the season and most people do not seek vaccination until October.

World.title: Ponzi schemer who defrauded Travis Kelce tried to marry U.S. citizen to avoid deportation, prosecutors say
World.content:
The undocumented Indian immigrant behind a multi-million dollar Ponzi scheme that defrauded Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce and other investors tried to marry an American citizen before he was sentenced this week to 11 years in prison, court records show.

Federal prosecutors opposed Siddharth Jawahar’s request to marry Caroline Tredway, saying he may be attempting “to obtain immigration status in the United States,” according to a Sept. 4 filing in the U.S. District Court for Eastern District of Missouri.

Jawahar’s lawyer, however, insisted his client was not engaging in “marriage fraud” and said Tredway was willing to buy a $25 wedding ring and spend another $75 on an “officiant” to perform the ceremony.

“The truth is, Mr. Jawahar very much hopes to stay here after his sentence and build a life with Caroline, and he plans to pursue any legal avenues to do so,” attorney Doug Passon stated in his Sunday response.

Passon also acknowledged both Jawahar and Tredway are aware that “given this case and his current immigration status, his ability to remain here is highly unlikely.”

The revelations came two days after the 38-year-old Indian national, who pleaded guilty to three counts of wire fraud in January, was sentenced to prison and ordered to repay $31 million in restitution to victims he defrauded from 2016 to 2023.

It was during this proceeding at the U.S. District Court in St. Louis that a prosecutor briefly mentioned that Kelce was one of Jawahar’s many high-profile victims. Kelce has not addressed the report publicly.

NBC reached out to Tredway, who lives near Cleveland, to find out if she and Jawahar are still intending to marry. She has not responded.

“I don’t have any comment on that, and find it wholly irrelevant to the issues at hand,” Passon said in an emailed response to NBC News.

But in a June 30 phone call that was monitored by authorities, Jawahar and Tredway discussed the implications of them getting married, court records revealed.

“What if you get deported?” Tredway asked.

“If you don’t marry me, I guess that might happen,” Jawahar replied.

During that same conversation, the records showed, Jawahar also told Tredway that “the chance of me getting deported goes down dramatically” if they tied the knot.

Tredway, in an August letter to the court, said they met in 2021 and “officially became romantic” in February 2023.

“That night, Sid voiced his interest in me and asked me out on a date for the next evening,” she wrote. “That date turned out to be the best date of both of our lives. Because we already had such a strong foundation of trust and friendship, we fell deeply in love very quickly.”

Tredway, in her letter, insisted that “legitimizing our marriage before he enters a federal facility is vital for our family.”

“I enter into this marriage with my eyes completely open to Sid’s legal situation,” Tredway wrote.

In subsequent conversations with Tredway’s relatives, Jawahar also said he expected to be sentenced to “close to time served” and that he would then “focus on getting a pardon because there were a lot of gross violations of the law.”

“But my move after that is — I’d most likely be teaching a class in business ethics at Fordham University,” he was recorded as saying.

Marrying a U.S. citizen was apparently not the only gambit by Jawahar to avoid a lengthy prison sentence.

Jawahar in August, according to prosecutors, paid a prominent Missouri political consulting firm called Axiom $10,000 to try and sway the judge presiding over the case by getting U.S. Rep. Sam Graves, a Missouri Republican, to write a letter of support on his behalf.

Axiom also engineered the publication of a favorable article about Jawahar in a local newspaper that did not mention he was awaiting sentencing for a scheme that resulted in what U.S. District Judge Zachary Bluestone called “enormous losses” for investors.

Jawahar also tried to coach a victim to give a favorable statement to authorities and sought to have his sister wipe his iPhone, prosecutors said.

Much of Jawahar’s past remains murky, but records show that he arrived in the U.S. from India around the time he began studying at the University of Texas in fall 2005.

Jawahar was a government and philosophy major and took classes as recently as spring 2012 but did not graduate with a degree, a spokesperson at the school said.

The U.S. attorney’s office, however, says Jawahar ran a Texas-based investment company called Swiftarc Capital LLC and carried out a classic Ponzi scheme, using money from new investors to repay older investors and to fuel an extravagant lifestyle.

Jawahar traveled on private jets, stayed at luxury hotels, went on spending sprees and had memberships at private clubs across the U.S.

From July 2016 to December 2023, Jawahar’s company took in more than $35 million but invested roughly $10 million, the prosecutor’s office said.

In addition to Kelce, Jawahar was reportedly able to lure other top athletes to invest in his venture capital fund.

That group, according to a Forbes article published June 14, 2021, included NBA players Gary Harris, Tim Hardaway Jr. and Mason Plumlee.

“I’m thankful for Sid bringing me in, taking me under his wing and believing in me,” Harris was quoted as saying of Jawahar.

NBC News reached out to their agents asking whether the NBA players lost any money as a result of their investing with Jawahar and whether they cooperated with the federal investigation. There was no response from their agents.

World.title: Toys ‘R’ Us is opening 120 new stores as grownup collectors fuel toy sales
World.content:
Some people never seem to grow up. A resurgent Toys “R” Us is hoping to take that fact to the bank.

The storied chain announced Thursday it was opening 120 standalone Toys “R” Us locations this holiday season. In total, 160 standalone stores will be open in time for Christmas, the company said. The chain is already featured at numerous Macy’s outlets across the country.

Expect to see many adults and even teens shopping for themselves at these locations, in addition to the usual holiday shopping for kids.

Toy sales among adult-only households have now outpaced households with children for toy sales, growing 16% through June, according to market research group Circana, equivalent to 55% of total toy industry receipts. Toy sales among all adults are growing 25%, only slightly behind the teen group at 33%. Together, teens and adults generated nearly 60% of the industry’s incremental dollar gains in the first half, Circana said.

The trends have helped toys see their strongest overall first-half-of-the-year sales in six years. It’s part of a broader trend toward so-called “analog” products in an increasingly digital world.

“We’re seeing toys increasingly function as hobbies, fandom ecosystems, and social experiences rather than traditional children’s products,” said Kristen McLean, vice president of client insights for Circana’s Entertainment Knowledge Group. “That’s expanding the consumer base and creating new opportunities for manufacturers and retailers that understand how to engage collectors, enthusiasts, gifters, and self-purchasers.”

Toys “R” Us didn’t mention adult collectors in its announcement.

The top toy brands today include Pokémon; major sports leagues like NFL, FIFA, and MLB; Marvel, Star Wars, Hot Wheels, and LEGO Botanicals, Circana said. Toys “R” Us named LEGO, Barbie, Hot Wheels, Pokémon, and KPop Demon Hunters as the top brands it plans to offer.

In its heyday, Toys “R” Us had more than 1,000 locations across the United States. But it filed for bankruptcy in 2017 as it was boxed out by larger rivals such as Walmart and Amazon amid a broader downturn in brick-and-mortar sales as e-commerce began to boom.

Today, Toys “R” Us is managed by WHP Global, a group backed by private equity that also oversees Babies “R” Us, as well as a suite of fashion brands including Express, Marc Jacobs and Vera Wang.
