World.title: Estonia enters ETS reform talks without setting numerical targets
World.content:
The Riigikogu's EU Affairs Committee (ELAK) clarified the government's mandate for negotiations on reforming the Emissions Trading System (ETS) at its meeting on Friday, but avoided setting any numerical parameters.

"We made significant corrections to the positions proposed by the government," ELAK chair Peeter Tali (Eesti 200) told ERR on Friday.

He said the mandate confirms three principles that must guide Estonia's negotiations: security of supply, security considerations, and socio‑economic impact.

"When we talk about the oil‑shale industry, security considerations in Ida‑Viru County also mean stability and employment for people. And security of supply — that we can still get energy and that our economy and industry can develop. We also highlighted the oil‑shale oil sector separately, stressing that it is important and must be kept alive as long as possible," Tali said.

Free emission allowances need to be retained longer

Energy and environment minister Erkki Keldo (Reform Party), who attended the meeting, gave ERR a more detailed overview of Estonia's aims in the ETS 1 reform.

"First, we have proposed — and the European Commission has also suggested — that free emission allowances should not decrease as quickly as previously planned. Estonia can agree with this. Our goal is to retain free allowances for as long as possible, both now and in the future — and as many as possible, to put it simply," Keldo said.

He noted that while free allocation was initially set to end in 2039, the timeline is now being extended to 2046–2047, and the reduction pace will slow. "For us, it is important that the first phase slows down as much as possible — that the reduction happens at a minimal pace so our sectors remain competitive," he said.

The new Enefit 280-2 oil shale plant in Auvere, Ida-Viru County. Source: Sergei Stepanov/ERR

Second, Keldo highlighted the need for greater price stability in ETS carbon allowances — something Estonian businesses have also requested, as sharp price swings make planning difficult.

"The idea of the reform is to give the CO₂ price more stability and predictability. The discussion is about automatically releasing additional units onto the market if the price per ton rises above a certain threshold, to stabilize it. The goal is a predictable price with less volatility," he said.

Keldo added that Estonia wants free allowances to cover the oil‑shale sector and that allocation must consider Estonia's specific circumstances — including security, socio‑economic impacts, and security of supply.

He also stressed Estonia's position that free allowances should take into account past investments that have already reduced emissions, rather than being tied only to future investments. Under the Commission's current proposal, free allowances would be granted only to companies that commit to future emission‑reduction investments.

Emissions reduction hindered by lack of technology

"As we know, it is not realistically possible to make many future investments in oil shale. And when we talk about innovation, such as carbon capture, it is extremely expensive and there are no economically viable technologies. We want to ensure our oil‑shale sector is not put at a disadvantage," Keldo said.

Peeter Tali. Source: Priit Mürk / ERR

Both Tali and Keldo emphasized that Estonia's positions were not defined numerically, so negotiators would not be overly constrained — especially since ETS decisions in the EU are made by qualified majority, meaning Estonia's exact numbers could simply be ignored.

"This is how the EU works — ETS reform does not require unanimity, only qualified majority. That means negotiations and finding common ground with other member states. That's why Estonia's positions clearly explain why we seek exceptions and what our needs are, but we have not locked ourselves into specific numbers or percentages," Keldo said.

"All principles are written into the government's positions, but we did not include exact percentages. I can say that the government's goal is to secure as many free allowances as possible for as long as possible for Estonian companies. That is the goal we will negotiate," he added.

Tali echoed the same: "The exact percentage is a matter of negotiation. Experienced negotiators say there is no point putting a number in, because then you're boxed in — and you need room to maneuver."

Both Tali and Keldo also stressed that all Estonian representatives — politicians and officials, government and opposition, and members of the European Parliament — must consistently explain Estonia's interests and specific circumstances in the EU.

World.title: Organizers seek way for signers to join expanded 2028 Song Celebration
World.content:
This week marked the official start of preparations for the XIV Youth Song and Dance Celebration and the XXIX Song and XXII Dance Celebration, taking place in summer 2028. Artistic director of the Song Celebration, Riivo Jõgi, said that some changes can be expected, and meetings are underway to find a suitable solution for sign‑language performers.

The 2028 festival will last a full week and a half, from June 30 to July 9. "This stems from the coronavirus pandemic. We decided to combine the youth festival tradition with the general Song Celebration tradition. That's why the festival is significantly longer than before," Jõgi explained.

The festival is titled "Olemise viis" ("Way of Being"). "The title was chosen to be multilayered and philosophical. One meaning could relate to what it means to be Estonian across time — a deeper underlying idea," Jõgi said.

"When writing the concept, I focused largely on time — who we have been in the past, who we are now, and what we leave to future generations. The Song Celebration will take place over three days, from Friday to Sunday. Previously it was held only on Saturday and Sunday. Spanning three days felt inspiring and compelling for expressing the passage of time," he noted.

Jõgi believes that this time the Sunday concert will not sell out far ahead of the others. "Each day has its own character. Friday is communal singing, Saturday features adult categories with wind orchestras under the arch, and Sunday is dedicated to children's categories. For the final combined choir, performers from the previous days join as well," he explained.

He emphasized that reaching the Song Celebration stage requires significant work. "But I'd even say that in the end, everyone can come to the Song Celebration. The real question is who gets under the arch and who listens. There is great magic in listening and being present at the festival. Sometimes it's even more wonderful to hear what is offered from under the arch," Jõgi said.

Jõgi noted that organizers have held meetings with sign‑language choirs, and discussions will continue in autumn. "We are trying to find a suitable way for them to participate in the Song Celebration," he said.

Among other changes, Jõgi highlighted the separation of mixed choirs and youth mixed choirs, as well as the separation of girls' and women's choirs.

"Since I'm more of an orchestra person and try to pay attention to those aspects, one difference compared to recent festivals is that on Friday we will use a wind orchestra as the accompanying ensemble. On Saturday and Sunday, a symphony orchestra. A lovely children's combined choir will also be formed — something we haven't done before — consisting of boys' choirs, young children's choirs, and children's choirs," Jõgi said.

World.title: Estonia seeks more stores to join emergency preparedness network
World.content:
Estonia has 60 emergency-ready gas stations and 79 stores equipped with generators in case of a power outage. By the end of the year, the number of such stores is expected to reach 110.

Estonia has more than 550 gas stations, around 10 percent of which have now been designated emergency-ready gas stations. Compared with other gas stations, they maintain larger fuel reserves and have generators for use in an emergency, Priit Ploompuu, a member of the management board of the Estonian Stockpiling Agency, said.

"We can say that already today there are around 60 gas stations with enhanced emergency preparedness that are able to dispense fuel during a power outage. That is more than 10 percent of all gas stations in Estonia. The designation comes with an obligation to maintain a reasonable reserve of fuel in the tanks at an emergency-ready gas station," Ploompuu said.

Estonia is expected to have 110 emergency-ready stores by the end of this year, but agreements have so far been signed with 79 stores. More volunteers are therefore needed to join the program and equip their stores with generators provided by the Estonian Stockpiling Agency.

"We have 31 generators waiting, so to speak, and we need partners who are willing to have them connected at their premises," Ploompuu said.

"I would call on all store owners, local government representatives or ordinary people who want an emergency-ready store near them to help move this project forward because we have a procurement process underway that stores can participate in," Ploompuu added.

World.title: Iraq Customs clarifies duties on pharmaceuticals, vitamins, and supplements
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi General Authority of Customs asserted on Friday evening, September 18, 2026, that the formal classification of imported commodities and the determination of their corresponding Harmonized System (HS) codes and tariff bands remain the exclusive legal jurisdiction of the customs authority.

In a statement received IraqiNews.com, the authority clarified the operative tariff schedules for healthcare products, noting that certified pharmaceutical products are levied at a baseline duty of 0.5%, while vitamins and dietary supplements face duties of either 5% or 10% based on technical categorization.

Customs regulators emphasized that receiving testing clearances or regulatory approvals from the Ministry of Health does not automatically classify a product as a pharmaceutical medicine for border assessment purposes.

The authority underlined that health sector certifications fulfill domestic safety compliance requirements, whereas border taxation, HS code designation, and duty assessments are determined strictly through official statutory tariff tables and active customs regulations.

Under the declared tariff structure, conventional pharmaceuticals formally categorized under recognized medical subheadings qualify for the lower 0.5% rate.

Conversely, vitamins and nutritional supplements are evaluated individually based on their specific chemical formulation, physical composition, and technical commodity descriptions, subjecting them to standard 5% or 10% duty brackets rather than pharmaceutical exemptions.

The authority reiterated that brand names, marketing designations, or laboratory review bodies do not dictate tariff bands, which rely solely on technical HS documentation.

The regulatory clarification addresses recurring friction between border revenue authorities and the domestic healthcare market regarding import costs. In January 2026, the General Authority of Customs confirmed a 1% tariff adjustment on medical supplies, dismissing claims of a ten-fold duty increase flagged by the Iraqi Syndicate of Pharmacists as an unintentional clerical error.

The latest customs advisory establishes clear statutory boundaries between health testing protocols and fiscal border valuations, maintaining firm oversight over revenue collection on non-essential health and wellness supplements entering the country.

World.title: Iraqi Election Commission monitors Russian elections in Moscow
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A senior delegation from Iraq’s Independent High Electoral Commission (IHEC), headed by the Chairman of the Board of Commissioners, Judge Omar Ahmed Mohammed, commenced official international election monitoring duties in the Russian Federation on Friday, September 18, 2026.

The delegation, which includes Chief Electoral Officer Hussein Abdul-Sada Baheer and Board of Commissioners member Abbas Farhan, is participating as accredited international observers for the Russian State Duma parliamentary elections running through September 20, following a formal invitation extended by the Central Election Commission of the Russian Federation.

IHEC confirmed in an official statement received by the 964 Network that the visit is designed to enhance institutional cooperation, facilitate knowledge exchange on electoral administration, and examine international frameworks for staging large-scale voting processes.

Alongside their direct oversight roles, the Iraqi delegation is taking part in the international forum entitled “Elections in Times of Turmoil,” an expert convening addressing technical, logistical, and administrative mechanisms required to organize and secure democratic balloting under exceptional operational constraints and shifting geopolitical realities.

As part of their official itinerary, the Iraqi commissioners initiated field inspection rounds across several designated polling stations to observe on-the-ground voting workflows firsthand.

The monitoring tour focused on evaluating voting machine operations, logistical organization, ballot management, and queue protocols inside voting centers. IHEC noted that participating in high-level overseas monitoring missions forms a core element of its strategy to benchmark international best practices, integrate comparative operational knowledge, and refine Iraq’s domestic technical and administrative capacities for future electoral cycles.

World.title: Iraq and France work on energy pipeline to Europe
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — France is working with Iraq and Jordan on a pipeline project to transport Iraqi oil and gas to European markets, French President Emmanuel Macron said days after Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi visited Paris for discussions on energy and investment.

Macron stated that the initiative was part of attempts to secure an alternate energy supply for Europe, since the Middle East crisis interrupts conventional shipping routes and raises oil and gas costs.

Iraqi official media said that the planned pipeline would take Iraqi energy via Jordan to European markets.

The statement comes after Al-Zaidi’s official visit to France from September 13 to 14, during which he met with Macron at the Élysée Palace.

The two leaders addressed diversifying energy supply pathways in the wake of delays to Iraqi oil shipments and increased pressure on global energy markets.

During the visit, Iraq and TotalEnergies, a French energy giant, agreed to initiate negotiations on further energy projects, including gas supply collaboration.

TotalEnergies is also looking for a share in the multinational consortium implementing the proposed Basra-Baniyas pipeline, which would give Iraqi petroleum an alternative route from southern oilfields to Syria’s Mediterranean coast, circumventing the Strait of Hormuz.

Chevron, TI Capital, and UCC Holdings of Qatar are all members of the partnership.

The projects highlight Iraq’s quickening efforts to diversify export routes after interruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, which revealed the risk of depending mainly on southern marine terminals for petroleum shipments.

Macron said that Middle Eastern turmoil has exacerbated Europe’s energy challenges, making alternative oil and gas suppliers even more crucial.

France is also advocating for more international cooperation on energy stockpiles and supply, while prices stay high.

For Iraq, new pipeline links via Jordan and Syria might give alternate routes to European clients while lessening its vulnerability to outages in the Arabian Gulf.

World.title: England can build on World Cup ‘spirit’, says Tuchel
World.content:
London – Thomas Tuchel said England will build on the “fantastic spirit” of their World Cup campaign as he targets glory on home soil at Euro 2028.

The England boss was speaking at Wembley after naming a 27-man group for a four-game Nations League camp, starting with a clash against world champions Spain on September 26.

It comes just nine weeks after the end of the World Cup, where England conceded two late goals in a painful semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold and Chelsea forward Cole Palmer were the headline picks after both were controversially overlooked for the World Cup.

Tuchel also included Liverpool’s teenage winger Rio Ngumoha, uncapped Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite in his first squad since the tournament in North America.

A number of players who were in the World Cup squad including John Stones, Djed Spence, Dan Burn, Jordan Henderson and Dean Henderson missed out through injury.

Former Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Tuchel said he did not see the Nations League as a new start, instead focusing on continuity.

“I feel that it’s not a new beginning that we are starting now, so we build on a solid and very valuable foundation, and the target is to win the home Euros,” he told reporters on Friday.

Euro 2028 will be co-hosted by England, Scotland, Wales, and Ireland.

The German said his side’s ultimate failure at the World Cup had left him unfulfilled but stuck by his squad picks.

“I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic,” he said.

“I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.”

Tuchel said Palmer had impressed for Chelsea early in the season.

“He has his numbers back, he has assists back, he has decisive goals back, so that’s why he’s in the squad and I think he has a point to prove,” he said.

“The same goes for Trent. He was never off the list, he was never in a non-selectable class, and he has this chance to show, to be the best version of himself.”

Tuchel said it was his “duty” to play Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo after he failed to feature for a single minute at the World Cup.

The England boss welcomed the challenge of taking on Spain at Wembley.

“We feel the gap is closing and we feel that we are close and we want a proof of point,” he said.

“The stadium is sold out, it will be very exciting, the motivation cannot be higher to play against the world champions.”

England also play the Czech Republic twice and Croatia once during the upcoming international window.

World.title: Anti-Assad music star makes triumphant return to Syria
World.content:
Damascus – Syrian singer Assala Nasri has made a triumphant return to Damascus with a sold-out concert following 15 years of exile due to her opposition to ousted ruler Bashar al-Assad.

Thousands of fans welcomed the 57-year-old, known mononymously as Assala, at a venue in the Syrian capital where she bowed and opened the show with songs hailing the Syrian people.

“Souls of my heart, I missed you,” she repeatedly said to endless cheers on Thursday night.

“My loves, my people, I swear, until this moment I could not believe that I am among you. I want to tell you how much I dreamt of this.”

There was a heavy security presence for the concert, after some religious conservatives launched a campaign calling for its cancellation.

Half of the show’s proceeds will be donated to charity.

Syria’s new Islamist authorities, who overthrew Assad in 2024, have welcomed Assala. Culture Minister Mohammed Yassine Saleh has dubbed her “the daughter of Damascus”.

Joining her on stage, he said her return was that of “every honest Syrian and every free person”.

– ‘Moving forward’ –

Assala was among the first artists to express support for the peaceful anti-Assad protests that erupted in 2011, refusing to partake in events supporting his government.

She was booted from the Syrian artists’ union for her stance and was the target of media campaigns.

She went into exile, living in Cairo with her family and playing shows in various Arab countries.

The bloody repression of the protests led to a 13-year civil war that killed more than half-a-million people.

At Assala’s show, small Syrian flags rippled in time with the music, with many in the crowd unable to hold back their tears.

“I never thought this day would come. It’s like a beautiful dream,” concert-goer Sawsan Wadha, 56, said.

“We are very happy that our country is moving forward,” added 40-year-old Lynn Nahas.

On her new record, “The Syrian Album”, Assala covers folk songs from all 14 of Syria’s provinces as an homage to her country’s cultural diversity.

She sings for the cities scarred by war, but also for the coastline in mourning after last year’s killing of hundreds of members of Assad’s Alawite minority, and for Druze-majority Sweida, which also saw sectarian violence.

– Recovery through art –

Assala’s piercing, powerful voice rang out as she made her way through the album’s tracks at Thursday’s concert.

She also performed fan favourites like “Samehtak” and “Sandooq”, with the jubilant, tearful crowd singing along.

Assala and her family only returned to Damascus this week. An antiques dealer in the capital returned the oud, or Oriental lute, that had belonged to her father, a celebrated musician.

Conservative Muslim figures had expressed criticism in the run-up to the concert.

Egyptian preacher Hani Dahab, who lives in Syria, launched a social media campaign with the slogan “Cancel the Sinful Concerts”. He accused the culture ministry of seeking to “give society a secular character”.

Syrian Salafi preacher Abdul Razzaq al-Mahdi condemned what he called a “concert of music and debauchery”, while a group of preachers in Damascus called on the culture minister to take into account “the religious identity of society”.

While not addressing the critics directly, Assala said at the show that “recovery will only happen with art and music”.

Syria has seen a cultural boom since 2025, but also the rise of preachers and conservative religious movements in public spaces and at universities, raising fears of restrictions on freedom.

Farah Al-Atassi, political advisor to the government, said poetry, language and thought were “an integral part of Syrian identity”.

“This is the Syria that we know and that will endure,” she told AFP.

World.title: UNESCO can be ‘moderator’ in AI debate: chief to AFP
World.content:
Paris – UNESCO chief Khaled el-Enany has proposed in an interview with AFP that the UN culture and education agency become a facilitator in the worldwide wrangling on the risks of artificial intelligence.

“I believe we are uniquely positioned to make UNESCO a true moderator in this global debate,” he said as he prepared to welcome Pope Leo XIV, a key advocate for international AI governance, in Paris next week.

The UN educational, scientific and cultural organisation has long stressed that its remit covers more than heritage, looking to advance in areas ranging from access to education to the ethical use of artificial intelligence.

The debate over the potential dangers of self-improving algorithms has surged in recent weeks, with some researchers warning the technology could end humanity, and leaders of AI companies suggesting development needed to be slowed down.

US President Donald Trump has on the other hand called the fears a “hoax”.

Enany told AFP: “There is a risk that it will get out of control if we don’t intervene.”

“This break, this dialogue that has taken place over the past few weeks, is something very positive,” he added in the interview on Thursday.

He said the cultural agency had found an “indispensable partner” in the pontiff, who is to visit the UNESCO headquarters in Paris on Friday next week at the start of a four-day trip to France.

“This visit will be the beginning of a very solid partnership to strengthen and protect human dignity in this industrial revolution,” Enany said.

It will be the first visit by a pope to UNESCO headquarters since John Paul II in 1980.

– AI ‘must be governed’ –

Pope Leo, the first US pope, this week warned against delegating to algorithms decisions that should be taken by humans alone.

In his first major document, the encyclical “Magnifica Humanitas” (Magnificent Humanity), published in May, the pope issued a call to “disarm” AI in order to “prevent it from dominating humanity”.

Enany said UNESCO had long been concerned with regulating AI, in 2021 issuing a “Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence”.

The guide warned about the risk of violations of privacy and the concentration of technological power in the hands of a few states or companies, and well as potential effects on democracy and the environment.

AI is “an extraordinary tool, but one that must be governed in an ethical, inclusive, and fair way,” Enany said.

Trump has since returning to office withdrawn the United States from UNESCO, alleging that it is biased against Israel and promotes “divisive” causes.

China — one of the major global AI players — has become the agency’s largest donor.

Trump had already ordered a departure from UNESCO in 2017 during his first term, before President Joe Biden reestablished US membership.

As the United States rejoined in 2023, then US secretary of state Antony Blinken said it was key Washington was present at UNESCO for decisions “that actually matter”, including on “rules, norms and standards for artificial intelligence”.

China was among countries to oppose the move.

World.title: Bahrain’s Ramsis Engineering expands into Iraq with Basra office
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Bahrain-based Ramsis Engineering has opened a new branch in Basra to serve Iraq’s growing energy and industrial sectors.

The new office will put the mechanical engineering firm closer to its clients and partners in southern Iraq, where the majority of the country’s oil, gas, and heavy industrial activities are located.

Ramsis stated that its Iraq operations would concentrate on manufacturing, maintenance, and specialized engineering services, building on its expertise in the oil and gas, petrochemical, aluminum, power, and desalination sectors.

The Basra opening establishes the company’s local foothold as Iraq invests in oilfield development, gas processing, and large industrial infrastructure.

Ramsis offers mechanical engineering, building, manufacturing, maintenance, and oilfield services to industrial operators.

World.title: Most Asian stocks track Wall St rally, yen drops after BoJ rate hike
World.content:
Hong Kong – Asian stocks mostly rose on Friday in line with a rally on Wall Street as a drop in oil prices eased inflation concerns, while the yen dropped against the dollar even after the Bank of Japan hiked interest rates to a three-decade high.

The Federal Reserve’s lift in borrowing costs this week provided some relief to traders concerned that policymakers were not moving quick enough to address a spike in inflation that could deal a blow to the world’s top economy.

That has been helped by news that Saudi Arabia was moving to restore within days about half of crude shipments disrupted by the stoppage of its East-West pipeline to the Red Sea.

The conduit, even more important since the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz by Iran, was shut last week after being targeted by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.

Crude prices, which had soared around a fifth in September, have fallen around five percent from recent highs, with West Texas Intermediate dipping below $100 for the first time since last Friday. WTI was down more than one percent Friday and Brent lost two percent.

The surge in oil this month has been among the main catalysts for rising inflation since the United States and Israel began their war on Iran at the end of February.

And the latest fall-off provided some much-needed support to stocks.

Seoul, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Taipei, Mumbai and Bangkok all advanced, although there were losses in Singapore, Wellington, Jakarta and Manila. Sydney was barely moved.

London, Paris and Frankfurt dipped.

The latest moves in oil and the Fed’s action reassured investors and kept the 10-year US Treasury bond yield — a key indicator of borrowing costs throughout the world’s biggest economy — back below five percent.

Japan’s Nikkei was also helped by a drop in the yen against the dollar that came in the wake of the BoJ’s well-telegraphed decision to lift rates to their highest level since 1995.

Pressure has increased on officials to further tighten monetary policy as a spike in oil prices caused by the Middle East crisis — which shows little sign of ending anytime soon — is expected to keep putting a floor under inflation.

“Given that underlying CPI inflation has been approaching two percent and financial conditions have been accommodative, the bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate,” the BoJ said on its website.

But the yen slipped to more than 157 to the greenback, compared with around 156 earlier.

Stephen Innes at Quintex Intel suggested traders were jolted by the fact that the hike was not unanimous, passing by a 7-2 majority.

“For a market looking for evidence that the BoJ could shorten the distance between hikes, those dissents mattered,” he wrote.

“Traders were looking for signs that the Bank could move faster from here, yet two members were already arguing that even today’s move had come too soon.”

Focus will now turn to Governor Kazuo Ueda’s news conference due later in the day.

“Attention should fall on the forward swaps curve and the Bank’s guidance around the pace and urgency of further tightening,” wrote Chris Weston at Pepperstone.

“The market will be looking for confirmation that further normalisation remains firmly on the table, while assessing whether the Bank sees any urgency to move again.”

World.title: 'Delhi a terrifying daily story for women': Rahul, Priyanka slam Amit Shah over teen's gangrape-murder
World.content:
Rahul directly questioned Shah over the responsibility for women's safety in Delhi. Priyanka Gandhi further questioned the government's response to crimes against women.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

What happened in Delhi case

NEW DELHI: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra have spoken out over the alleged gang rape and murder of a teenage girl in Delhi, with both questioning the authorities over women's safety and demanding accountability for the incident.Rahul Gandhi, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, criticised the Delhi Police and questioned the responsibility of Union home minister Amit Shah, under whose ministry the force functions. He said the teenager was gang-raped and murdered before her body was dumped in an open field, and questioned how the police remained unaware of the crime for days.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi described the incident as a "horrific act of brutality" in the national capital. He also dismissed the idea that Delhi was providing women with a safe environment, saying the city had instead become a source of fear for women."It's unfortunate that Delhi is no longer the capital today; it has become a terrifying daily story for women," he said.Rahul directly questioned Shah over the responsibility for women's safety in Delhi. He pointed out that the Delhi Police is under the Union home ministry and asked who should ultimately be held responsible for the safety of women in the capital."Amit Shah ji, Delhi Police is under your control. Ultimately, whose responsibility is women's safety?" he said.He also criticised the functioning of the Delhi Police, asking whether its role had been reduced to intimidating ordinary citizens while criminals continued to operate without fear."Or has the job of Delhi Police been reduced to just intimidating and threatening ordinary citizens? Because the criminals are roaming around fearlessly," Gandhi said.Calling for immediate action, the Congress leader demanded that those responsible for the crime be arrested and punished strictly. He also sought accountability for what he described as criminal negligence."The beasts must be arrested immediately, strict action and punishment must be taken, and accountability for this criminal negligence must be fixed," he said.Rahul Gandhi ended his post by linking women's safety to India's wider progress, saying, "India cannot move forward without women's safety."Priyanka Gandhi also raised concerns over the case, saying the crime against the teenager represented an extreme form of brutality. She noted that another minor girl had allegedly been raped just days earlier and questioned whether authorities were taking sufficient responsibility for women's safety."In Delhi, all limits of cruelty were crossed against a 17-year-old girl, and after that, she was brutally murdered. Just a few days earlier, another minor girl was raped," she said in a post on X.Priyanka Gandhi further questioned the government's response to crimes against women. She argued that while there was discussion about women's development, women continued to face violence without what she described as concrete action against perpetrators."No one in the country is willing to take responsibility for women's safetyâonly empty talk about women's development is offered," she said.She claimed that hundreds of women face atrocities and violence and alleged that victims can struggle to get action from authorities, including the registration of FIRs."Hundreds of women face atrocities and violence, but they cannot hope for concrete action against the perpetratorsâFIRs aren't even filed," she said.Priyanka Gandhi also said the issue went beyond the individual case and reflected a wider failure to ensure women's basic rights. She argued that both society and the government had failed to provide women with adequate safety, freedom and equality."Both society and the government have completely failed in granting women their rights to safety, freedom, and equality," she said.A teenage girl was allegedly gang-raped and murdered in Delhi. Her body was subsequently dumped in an open field, with the police facing questions over the delay in detecting the crime.The case has triggered political criticism over women's safety in the capital, with Rahul Gandhi focusing on the Delhi Police's role and its accountability to the Union home ministry.Priyanka Gandhi also referred to another case involving a minor girl that was reported days before the teenager's rape and murder. She used the two incidents to question the wider response to crimes against women.

World.title: Ladakh groups call off week-long protest march
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Ladakhi political groups have called off the proposed week-long protest march in the region and said they will instead hold a "symbolic" one-day march on Sept 23, citing weather conditions and changing political situation in the UT.

"Due to prevailing weather conditions with cold nights, we're making it into a symbolic 20-km march on Sept 23, followed by martyrs' day event on Sept 24. Inconvenience regretted, look forward to joining you and marching together," said climate activist Sonam Wangchuk, of Leh Apex Body, one of the two outfits that have been representing Ladakh in talks with Centre on demands for the region.

World.title: US national gets default bail in terror case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A special NIA court in Delhi Friday granted default bail to the US national arrested in March on terror charges for allegedly helping ethnic armed groups in India and Myanmar, days after the "incomplete" chargesheet filed by the investigating agency dropped charges under UAPA, reports Koushiki Saha.

While granting bail to Matthew Aaron VanDyke, who has spent 180 days in custody, the court noted NIA's failure to complete its probe. It cannot be concluded that the accused is not entitled to default bail merely because an agency says a probe is far from over, the court said.

VanDyke had sought default bail Thursday, contending that under Section 43D(2) proviso (1) of the anti-terror law, the investigation was required to be completed within 180 days, which ended on Sept 8.

World.title: MHA cites internal security issues to defend FCRA tweak
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Amid the charge from the opposition that Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill targets institutions run by minorities, especially Christians, Union home ministry asserted Friday that the amendments do not regulate charity but the entry of foreign money into a "sovereign space", which Centre is fully entitled to protect, and emphasised the law at its core is a "national-security" legislation.

A team of MHA officials led by home secretary Govind Mohan briefed the joint committee of Parliament - which is scrutinising the bill and held its first meeting - on different facets as it faced questions from MPs, with Mohan insisting the bill is not against any community, sources aware of the details said.

He said concerns over national interest, internal security and law and order are the main drivers of the bill. It was introduced by govt in Parliament's budget session and sent to the committee for scrutiny amid stiff protests from opposition parties and Christian groups, who had met home minister Amit Shah to convey their concerns.

After the meeting, the panel's chairperson, Sanjay Jaiswal, expressed confidence that it would be able to submit its report in the winter session of Parliament.

MPs from BJP-led NDA and opposition parties presented conflicting views.

BJP's Nishikant Dubey suggested India had a history of foreign money being used to influence issues of national interest and asked why Ford Foundation was allotted prime property in Lodhi Estate when over 1,400 NGOs linked to foreign funding were closed down under different laws before FCRA was enacted in 1976.





Rockefeller Foundation was a key financial support behind an elite cultural and intellectual organisation in central Delhi, he said.

Sources said DMK's P Wilson reiterated the charge that the amendments target Christian groups, which make up the majority of religious organisations with an FCRA licence, and was supported by other opposition MPs. Some alleged that these organisations were being targeted as they had empowered Dalits and women in south India.

Opposition MPs slammed the proposed amendments as draconian, saying even if an organisation surrendered its FCRA licence, it still allowed assets to be seized.

Jaiswal, sources said, flagged protests against the Kudankulam nuclear plant in TN and Sardar Sarovar Dam in Gujarat. BJP circles have argued that foreign-funded NGOs tried to disrupt the two critical projects of national interest under the veneer of environmental concerns.

According to data shared by MHA, TN has the highest number of organisations with FCRA registration (2,102), followed by Maharashtra (1,578), Karnataka (1,355) and Delhi (1,218). Foreign contribution increased to Rs 22,974 crore in 2024-25 from Rs 17,832 crore in 2015-16.

Out of the total foreign contribution received in 2024-25, 57% (Rs 13,071 crore) was for social purposes, 30% (Rs 6,933 crore) for educational, and only 8% (Rs 11,841 crore) for religious. Under the head of religious purpose, 73% went to Christian groups followed by 17.8% for Hindu organisations, with a little over 1% to Muslims. US and UK at Rs 12,113 crore and Rs 2,414 crore respectively were the two highest contributors.

World.title: CJP joins Rahul, says EC 'fixing' on behalf of BJP
World.content:
Saurav Das called for a wider political battle to hold Election Commission to account

NEW DELHI: Slamming the freezing of TMC symbol and name as "fixing" on behalf of BJP, Rahul Gandhi and CJP co-convener Saurav Das Friday called for a wider political battle to hold Election Commission to account - their programmatic convergence and acerbic tone raising prospects of a Jantar Mantar-like protest.Reactions came in late evening from the CPM general secretary MA Baby and the CPI(M-L)L general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya.While Baby told TOI that EC "doesn't have a reputation of impartiality any more", Bhattacharya claimed what EC has done is "wrong" and "now with Congress candidate arrested, there is a walkover-like situation for BJP". Bhattacharya's remarks were related to the TMC candidate for the Oct 6 Nandigram bypoll withdrawing after the EC order and Congress nominee's arrest.Taking a jibe at EC, Das said, "'Envelope' symbol for TMC defectors. Envelope me bharr ke kya aaya tha? (what came filled in the envelope?)."Rahul said, "Shiv Sena, NCP, and now TMC. Every time, the same pattern - BJP and EC join forces to split a party. Then its poll symbol is snatched away. Vote chori, govt chori and now party chori - these have become symbols of our democratic decline."

World.title: New symbols: Mamata gets 'football player', 'envelope' for rebel bloc
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Election Commission, a day after it temporarily froze Trinamool Congress' 'flowers and grass' poll symbol in view of the split in party, allotted a new set of party names and symbols to the rival factions led by

and Arup Roy.

EC approved the name 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress' for the group led by Mamata and allotted it the 'football player' poll symbol. The rival faction led by Arup was allotted the name 'Democratic Trinamool Congress' and 'envelope' poll symbol. The commission, in its order issued Friday, said it shall treat both the factions as recognised political parties in the states of West Bengal, Meghalaya and Tripura.

The new party names and symbols for Trinamool factions paved the way for their respective candidates to contest the Oct 6 bypoll to Nandigram and Rejinagar assembly seats in Bengal as well as Nagaon parliamentary seat in Assam. In Rejinagar, the Mamata faction had fielded Rabiul Alam Chodhury, and the Arup faction had fielded Saifuzzaman Sheikh as an AITC candidate.

Similarly, in Nandigram, the Mamata faction authorised Sanchita Pradhan as the AITC candidate, while the Arup faction signed the nomination papers for Ehteshmul Haque.





In Nagaon, the Mamata faction fielded Abdul Salam as an AITC candidate. EC Friday said bereft of its intervention, the returning officers would be bound to reject the nomination papers of candidates fielded by both factions, in view of the interim freeze on AITC's reserved symbol.

This, they said, would "deprive the electors of a fair electoral competition and prejudice the outcome of elections". World.title: Nitin Nabin donates 3 month's salary for flood relief in Bihar
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP chief Nitin Nabin Friday donated three months of his salary as Rajya Sabha MP to help efforts to aid flood victims in his home state Bihar, and asserted central and state govts are making every effort to deal with the crisis.

Expressing concern over the flood situation, he said Bihar govt is taking swift action and making adequate arrangements for relief camps, community kitchens, medical facilities and fodder for livestock in the affected areas.

Nabin said Centre and state stand fully committed to supporting the flood-affected families. Every possible assistance, including financial aid, relief camps, and crop damage assessment, is being extended to them, he said. "Fulfilling his responsibility during this time of crisis, he donated Rs 6.35 lakh, three months of his salary as an RS MP, to CM's Relief Fund," a BJP statement said.

Nabin also mentioned that Bihar govt has so far provided financial assistance totalling over Rs 550 crore to flood-affected families, at a rate of Rs 7,000 per family.

World.title: 25% youths in 250 districts not in education or jobs: Survey
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In nearly 250 districts, more than 25% youth (15-29 age group) are neither engaged in any productive work, nor are they pursuing education or any sort of training for work, highlighting a gap in human capital utilisation.

The situation is of particular concern in northern India, especially in states such as Bihar, UP, Haryana, Punjab and West Bengal, where nearly two-thirds of districts have around a quarter of the young population categorised as NEET (not in employment, education or training), showed the first-ever district-level periodic labour force survey (PLFS) for 2025, released by statistics ministry Friday.

In Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Assam and Telangana in nearly half the districts, 25% young population is categorised as NEET (not in employment, education or training).

A recent Niti Aayog report pegged the number of NEET youth in the country at nearly nine crore, with govt clarifying that these people cannot be crudely termed as unemployed.

In around 25 districts, NEET is below 10%, including Kabirdham, Rajnandgaon and Uttar Baster Kanker in Chhattisgarh; Chamba in Himachal Pradesh; Ernakulam in Kerala; and Mandla in Madhya Pradesh. Nabarangpur in Odisha had the lowest NEET rate of 4.1%.

The ministry's report covered around 600 districts in major states and UTs. In some cases, it clubbed a few adjoining districts and treated them as a single unit.

Lowest unemployment rates across India

Generally, high unemployment rate among youth is attributed to their participation in education or their engagement with skilling or vocational programmes. NEET, however, represents those people who are not enrolled anywhere with any educational institution and have also withdrawn from the labour force altogether. This is either due to them attending to domestic unpaid duties, care work in the case of women or those who have stopped looking for work due to no suitable work being available, or in some cases, preparing for exams or having leisure.

For young women, nearly three-fourth of total districts surveyed recorded a NEET rate of more than 25%, highlighting the burden of unpaid domestic chores and societal expectations.

World.title: Nepal disaster impact: Sikkim High Court initiates PIL on climate justice
World.content:
GUWAHATI

The High Court of Sikkim has initiated a suo motu public interest litigation (PIL) on climate justice after “taking note of the severe hardship and impact of the recent flash floods in Nepal”.

The flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, left 1,410 people dead and 6,145 still missing in northern and central Nepal.

In an order on September 17, a Bench comprising Chief Justice A. Muhamed Mustaque and Justice Bhaskar Raj Pradhan made the Railway Ministry and National Highways and Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited (NHIDCL), along with the Sikkim State Disaster Management Authority and the State Power Department, respondents in the PIL on “climate justice”.

The court issued notices to these four authorities.

The court said the PIL was initiated after it noted the impact of the disaster in Nepal, whose Himalayan landscape is similar to Sikkim’s. According to its order, the Chief Justice explained the grounds for initiating the proceedings in a detailed note.

“At the outset, the court considers it imperative to hear the public and potentially local communities who are likely to be affected by providing an accessible platform for them to voice their concerns,” the order reads.

The court appointed three legal experts as amici curiae to help it examine the issues arising from the proceedings, and listed the matter for the next hearing on October 6.

Sikkim has been a disaster-prone State, with hydropower, highways, and tunnelling projects said to make it more fragile. More than 1,200 people have died between the “Great Sikkim Floods” in October 1968 and the South Lhonak glacial lake outburst flood in October 2023.

World.title: What are the alternatives to SWIFT, and how are they faring? Explained
World.content:
The story so far: The New Delhi Declaration that came out of the recent BRICS Summit in the national capital resolved to increase trade between member-countries and payments in national currencies. Days before the summit, a report by the news agency Reuters quoted sources as saying that at the event, India would push to link central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) for cross-border payments across BRICS nations, despite political and technical hurdles that could limit progress. The proposal to link CBDCs would be part of the agenda for the leaders’ meeting, the sources said, though the limited adoption of digital currencies globally could complicate implementation, the report added. The proposal was, however, not part of the Declaration.

On the summit eve, Russia’s largest bank Sberbank said it saw major ‌opportunities for India-Russia bilateral trade settlements through CBDCs. At a media briefing in New Delhi, Sberbank chief executive officer Herman Gref said trade settlement in CBDCs was much ‌more efficient.

Multiple wars and U.S. weaponisation of the dollar through financial sanctions are making countries in the Global South think of bypassing the so-far universally accepted SWIFT system for inter-country payments. The attempts to do so have been patchy, but there is an increasingly felt need to have other options. Even on Thursday, the U.S. Senate empowered President Donald Trump to impose 100% tariffs on countries such as India and China that buy Russian oil or gas.

What are some of the alternatives to the Belgium-based SWIFT payment system?

Project mBridge is a group comprising the Bank of Thailand, the Central Bank of the United Arab Emirates, the Digital Currency Institute of the People’s Bank of China, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, and the Saudi Central Bank.

The Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS), a Reuters report said, is backed by the People’s Bank of China. China launched the CIPS clearing and settlement services system in 2015 to internationalise yuan use. It allows global banks to clear cross-border yuan transactions directly onshore, instead of through clearing banks in offshore yuan hubs, the report said.

The System for Transfer of Financial Messages, or SPFS, was developed by Russia in 2014 to bypass Western sanctions. In 2022, Russian banks were cut off from SWIFT, and the SPFS was of help.

SEPAMA, Iran’s local interbank telecom system, has as many as 52 branches of Iranian banks and four unnamed foreign banks connect ing with 106 banks using the SPFS, the Central Bank of Iran said in 2023.

How are these systems faring?

The Bank for International Settlements (BIS), an international financial institution owned by central banks to foster international monetary and financial cooperation, exited Project mBridge on October 31, 2024, after hand-holding it since 2019, when the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Bank of Thailand launched the system. mBridge, a cross-bloc multi-CBDC platform with no Western bank, attained minimum viability status in 2024. It was envisaged for direct peer-to-peer CBDC settlement without going through correspondent banks. The project team developed a new blockchain — the mBridge Ledger — custom-built by central banks to serve as a specialised and flexible platform for implementation of multi-currency cross-border payments in CBDCs, the BIS website says.

The BIS’s exit came under a cloud, with media reports saying it was because mBridge could provide the basis for a BRICS initiative to circumvent sanctions on Russia. A May 2016 Forbes report said that by late 2025, mBridge was in practice “a renminbi-denominated wholesale settlement rail for trade between China and the Gulf, running outside the dollar correspondent system”.

The remnimbi’s inclusion in the basket of currencies making up the Special Drawing Right, an international reserve asset created by the International Monetary Fund, has increased the acceptance of CIPS, which currently has participants in more than 120 countries, including all BRICS members with the exception of India, said a November 2025 opinion piece in The Hindu by Biswajit Dhar, a trade economist and former Professor, Jawaharlal Nehru University.

A March 19, 2026 South China Morning Post report says CIPS processed 679.8 billion yuan ($98.7 billion) of transactions on average per day in 2025, just a fraction of the $1.9 trillion of domestic and international payments Chips settles each business day. “While the CIPS has gained ground — especially among China’s trading partners in Africa and Asia — it remains far smaller in scale than established global systems, such as the U.S.-based Clearing House Interbank Payments System (Chips),” the report said. Beijing now appears to be moving towards building CIPS into a global platform compliant with multi-currency settlements and other foreign payment channels, the report quoted a study led by Ju Jiandong, a chair professor at Tsinghua University’s PBC School of Finance.

The SPFS, formed as Russian entities were banned from SWIFT, has grown at a record pace in 2023, the Russian central bank said that year, as Moscow ramped up efforts to resolve financial shortcomings wrought by sanctions over the Ukraine war. Alla Bakina, director of the central bank’s national payment system department, said 50 new entities had joined Russia’s alternative system that year, taking the total number to 440, of which more than 100 are non-residents.

The SPFS has been linked with Iran’s SEPAM, and entities in the Russian network can connect with Iranian banks.

How do India-Russia trade settlements happen now?

Russia and India, the second-largest importer of Russian oil, have built a functioning payments infrastructure using roubles and rupees, which now account for 96% of ‌bilateral trade, Ivan Nosov, head of Sberbank in India, said. “There are no problems with settlements between Russia and India. I am ready to say that this is one of the most reliable and best-established mechanisms for Russia’s payments with other countries,” he said.

According to official data, 22 Russian banks, including ⁠Sberbank, Russia’s largest lender, which was tasked with developing the payments infrastructure, and 17 Indian banks are currently servicing bilateral trade, a Reuters report said.

World.title: Can a Muslim minor marry under personal law? What courts have said | Explained
World.content:
The story so far: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has observed that under Muslim personal law, a person who has attained puberty is presumed to be competent to marry a person of their choice.

The observation came while the court was hearing a petition filed by a Muslim couple seeking protection of their life and liberty after marrying against the wishes of the woman’s family.

The judgment highlights an ongoing legal question concerning the interplay between personal laws and statutory child-protection frameworks, such as the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 (PCMA) and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences, 2012 (POCSO) Act. Under the PCMA, a “child” means a male who has not completed 21 years of age or a female who has not completed 18 years of age. A “child marriage” is a marriage to which either of the contracting parties is a child.

What was the case?

Justice Vikram Aggarwal made the observation while dealing with a petition filed by a 26-year-old Muslim man and a 17-year-and-eight-month-old Muslim woman, who sought protection from the woman’s family. The couple said they had performed nikah after the woman’s father opposed their relationship.

The court also observed that “As per Muslim Personal Laws, a boy or girl who has attained the age of puberty, which happens to be 15 years, is at liberty to marry anyone of his or her liking”.

What does Muslim personal law say?

The high court referred to Article 195 of Sir Dinshah Fardunji Mulla’s Principles of Mohammedan Law, which recognises a Muslim of sound mind who has attained puberty as competent to enter into a marriage contract. In the absence of evidence establishing an earlier or later attainment of puberty, the legal presumption operates from the age of 15 years.

The court also relied on its earlier decision in Kammu v. State of Haryana (2010), wherein it had held that a Muslim boy or girl who has attained puberty is at liberty to marry a person of their choice, and that a guardian cannot interfere with such a choice where the requirements of the applicable law are satisfied.

What have courts ruled over the years?

When it comes to Muslim personal law and the question of marriage of minors, different high courts have shown different opinions over the period of time.

In Mohd. Samim v. State Of Haryana, decided by the Punjab & Haryana High Court on September 26, 2018, the court examined the validity of the marriage between a man and a 16-year-old girl at the time of marriage. The petitioner argued that under Muslim Personal Law, the marriage was valid and that the PCMA did not apply. After considering various precedents and legal provisions, the court concluded that the marriage was valid under Muslim law, as the girl had attained puberty and was considered a major under Muslim Personal Law. Consequently, the court directed her release from a Safe House, allowing her to reside with her husband.

In Rahul v. State of Karnataka (2021), the Karnataka High Court noted that the POCSO Act will have an overriding effect on Muslim personal law.

The issue was considered again in Aleem Pasha v. State of Karnataka (2022). The Karnataka High Court observed that the POCSO Act is a special legislation to protect children from sexual offences and therefore, it will have an overriding effect on Muslim personal law. The court noted that a person will be held guilty of penetrative sexual assault under the POCSO Act if the wife is under the age of 18, even if the sexual intercourse took place in the course of the marriage. The petitioner, who was seeking bail, argued that since the girl had reached puberty in the present case and that Mohammedan law treats reaching puberty as a consideration for marriage at the age of 15, there had been no violations. The high court strongly disagreed with this argument, stating that the POCSO Act overrides personal law and that the age for engaging in sexual activity is 18 years.

SC notice on NCPCR plea

In October 2022, the Supreme Court issued notice on a plea by the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) seeking examination of the question arising from a Punjab and Haryana High Court ruling concerning a Pathankot-based Muslim couple, who had married under Muslim rites and sought protection from their families. But the Supreme Court declined to interfere with the relief granted to the couple. The High Court’s ruling had stemmed from a petition by Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, representing the NCPCR. He urged the court to stay the high court’s observations, terming it a “serious issue” in view of the statutory prohibition of child marriages.

The Supreme Court in January 2023 had also stated that the judgment of the Punjab and Haryana High Court in Javed v. State of Haryana and Others (2022), which had held that a Muslim girl aged 15 years can enter into a legal and valid marriage as per personal law, should not be relied upon as a precedent in any other case.

In Moidutty Musliyar v. State of Kerala, 2024, the Kerala High Court refused to quash proceedings against the persons accused of conducting a child marriage and facing offences under Sections 10 and 11 of the PCMA. The accused had argued that the Muslim personal law would apply to the parties and not the provisions of the Act. The court rejected the plea.

In Rubi v. State of U.P. 2026, the Allahabad High Court held that Muslim personal law recognising puberty as the age of marriage cannot override statutory provisions like the PCMA and the POCSO, which criminalise sexual relations with a child and provide protections to children.

However, on August 19, 2025, the Supreme Court dismissed a petition filed by the NCPCR challenging the 2022 judgment of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, which held that under Muslim personal law, a girl who has attained puberty or is aged 15 years and above, could marry, notwithstanding the provisions of the POCSO Act. The High Court had also extended protection to the couple against threats to their life and liberty. A Bench of Justices B.V. Nagarathna and R. Mahadevan ruled that the Commission lacked the locus standi to assail the High Court’s order.

What happened in the current case?

The latest Punjab and Haryana High Court order did not finally determine whether the 17-year-old’s marriage was valid. It dealt with the couple’s request for protection and referred to the position under Muslim personal law.

The court directed the Senior Superintendent of Police (Rural), Ludhiana, to consider the couple’s August 30 representation and take appropriate action, if required, in accordance with law. The petition was disposed of with these directions.

The broader legal question — how the position of Muslim personal law interacts with statutory protections for children — remains contested across courts.

World.title: What does the new U.S.-Denmark deal over Greenland entail, after Trump’s takeover threats?
World.content:
The United States, Denmark, and Greenland have reached an agreement that will allow the U.S. to develop a significant military presence in Greenland, while preventing U.S. adversaries from establishing bases on the island, U.S. President Donald Trump said on Friday (September 18, 2026).

The agreement comes after months of Mr. Trump threatening to take control of the island from Denmark by force.

Denmark and Greenland, an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark, welcomed the agreement and said it would be signed on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York next week.

Trump hails U.S.-Greenland deal

In a post on Truth Social, the U.S. President said no U.S. adversary would be able to make sensitive investments on the island without Washington’s approval, adding that the agreement had no expiry date.

“At my direction, we worked with representatives of Denmark and Greenland to guarantee that the United States will FOREVER have the complete ability to do what is necessary in Greenland in order to secure and defend the security of Greenland, and the United States of America,” Mr. Trump wrote. “This is a dream come true for the United States of America,” he added.

The announcement suggests that Mr. Trump may not revive his territorial claims over Greenland, at least in the near future. He said, without elaborating, that the U.S. would soon establish a significant military presence on the island, which already hosts a Space Force base in its remote northwest.

Mr. Trump, however, provided no details on how the agreement would work, and it was not immediately clear whether it was linked to, or substantially different from, the framework he had earlier said was reached following talks with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte.

Denmark, Greenland welcome deal

The office of Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said the agreement with the U.S. would be signed by the three governments next week during the United Nations General Assembly. However, parliamentary approval is still required from Denmark and Greenland before it can be implemented.

The Prime Minister’s office said the agreement would strengthen security in the North Atlantic and the Arctic.

In a statement, Ms. Frederiksen said “the agreement recognises the sovereignty and territorial integrity” of Greenland and Denmark and upholds both peoples’ right “to self-determination”.

Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen said the emerging agreement benefited all three governments and “recognises Greenland’s interests and our place in the international cooperation”. He also said the agreement with the United States “strengthens” the territory’s security.

Deal addresses U.S. security concerns

In a separate statement, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the agreement “permanently and completely” addressed Washington’s national security concerns regarding the island. “Greenland will forever be part of the strategic defense area of North America and exclude any adversary from it and the surrounding area,” he wrote.

The U.S. already has extensive overflight and basing rights in Greenland under a 1951 treaty. The defence agreement, updated in 2004, allows Washington to increase troop deployments and military installations on the island, provided it informs Denmark and Greenland in advance.

A State Department official, speaking on condition of anonymity to discuss specific terms, said the agreement prohibits non-NATO countries from establishing a base in Greenland and would allow only the U.S. and its allies to make unspecified “sensitive investments”.

The official said the agreement grants the U.S. permanent access, basing and overflight rights and would continue to apply even if Greenland becomes independent.

Strategic importance of Greenland

Mr. Trump has claimed that the U.S. needs Greenland to deter threats from Russia and China and has repeatedly alleged that Chinese and Russian military forces are operating near the island’s coastline.

Greenland has long been strategically important to the defence of North America. The U.S. maintained several bases and military installations on the island during the Cold War before scaling back its presence.

The U.S. continues to operate the remote Pituffik Space Base in northwestern Greenland, which was established after Washington and Copenhagen signed the Defense of Greenland Treaty in 1951. The facility supports missile warning, missile defence and space surveillance operations for the U.S. and NATO.

Greenland lies off the northeastern coast of Canada, with more than two-thirds of its territory within the Arctic Circle. Its geographical location has made the island strategically important to the defence of North America since World War II, when the U.S. occupied Greenland to prevent it from falling into the hands of Nazi Germany and to protect vital North Atlantic shipping routes.

Trump’s threats to take over Greenland

The agreement announced by Mr. Trump appears to mark a significant retreat from his earlier calls for the United States to take control of the autonomous Danish territory. Those demands drew strong opposition from European allies and presented one of the gravest challenges to the NATO alliance since the end of World War II.

Mr. Trump had repeatedly called on Denmark to sell Greenland to the United States, insisting that the island was crucial to U.S. security. He also refused to rule out taking control of the island through military force, despite Denmark being a NATO ally of the U.S.

Denmark and Greenland repeatedly said the island was not for sale and condemned reports that the U.S. was gathering intelligence there. Washington’s push for control of Greenland also faced strong opposition from Russia and much of Europe.

Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Mr. Trump has repeatedly insisted that Washington needs control of Greenland for strategic reasons. He has made veiled threats to seize the island by force and raised the prospect of higher tariffs on goods from European countries that did not support his position.

The pressure campaign reached a head in January 2026 during the World Economic Forum in Davos, where Mr. Trump criticised European allies in his address. He later backed away from his demands following talks with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, saying instead that the two sides had agreed on the parameters of a framework concerning Greenland and the Arctic region.

World.title: CMRL-Exalogic pay-off case: Keralam Advocate General recommends FIR registration against Pinarayi, daughter Veena, Riyas
World.content:
The top legal officer of the Keralam government is understood to have advised the State government to accept the report of the Directorate of Enforcement, which accused the former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter T. Veena, her husband P.A. Mohamed Riyas and a few others in the CMRL-Exalogic pay-off case of engaging in money laundering, and register a first information report (FIR).

The ED had submitted the report to the State Police Chief last week seeking to initiate further action in the case. The investigation agency had reportedly arrived at a conclusion that the accused, including Mr. Vijayan, Mr. Riyas and Ms. Veena, were involved in money laundering in association with Sasidharan Kartha, the managing director of Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited, and his associates.

K. Jaju Babu, the Advocate General, is understood to have advised the registration of the FIR against all those named in the report and to invoke provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act. The police authority is legally bound to accept the report under Section 66 (2) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 and proceed with register the FIR, in the wake of the principles laid down by the Supreme Court, sources indicated.

A final call on the follow-up action on the ED report will be taken after a meeting of the Advocate General with State Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan. The AG had earlier sought reports from the Additional Advocate General and the Director General of Prosecution on various aspects of the case, sources indicated.

On its part, the ED shared the information with the State police by invoking Section 66 (2) of the Act, which states that if the director is of the opinion that the provisions of any other law for the time being in force are contravened, then the director shall share the information with the agency concerned for necessary action. The scope of further action on the report in the CMRL-Exalogic payoff case was discussed based on the recent judgments of the Supreme Court, sources indicated.

Incidentally, a few political leaders, including the State Ministers, had earlier admitted that they had received funds from Mr. Kartha after a diary noting on the payments had surfaced. The leaders had played down the receipt of money as a case of collection of funds from an industrialist for their respective political parties. A section of political leaders had also demanded a probe into the money received by these leaders.

Incidentally, it came to light over the past few days that Mr. Kartha and the former CFO of CMRL had retracted their statements given to ED, which formed the basis of the case. The duo had also accused the ED of arm-twisting them to give false evidence against politicians.

World.title: Trump bans media outlets CNN, MS NOW, Politico from White House
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump said on Friday (September 18, 2026) he was banning news outlets CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, accusing them without specifics of reporting “fiction and lies.”

“I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW... and Politico... from the White House as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!” Mr. Trump said on his Truth Social network.

He said that he ‌might ‌bar ⁠other ⁠media outlets ​from ‌the White House.

It follows Mr. Trump’s decision in February 2025 to keep The Associated Press journalists out of the Oval Office, Air Force One and other events too small for a full press corps, in retaliation for the news outlet’s decision not to follow his lead in changing the Gulf of Mexico’s name.

The AP filed suit, and the case is ongoing.

Mr. Trump has long bristled at news coverage he sees as unfavourable to him and has a history of filing lawsuits against news organisations and lashing out at individual reporters in person or over social media.

Since returning to office, Mr. Trump has pursued legal action against The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, the BBC and other news outlets.

With AFP, Reuters, AP inputs

World.title: 31 dead in attack at police headquarters in Pakistan
World.content:
At least 31 died from an explosion and gun attack at a police headquarters in northern Pakistan, a senior police official told AFP on Saturday (September 19, 2026), with fighting ongoing.

Attackers stormed the Old Police Lines complex at Kohat, a town of around 2,20,000 people in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province, on Friday (September 18, 2026) afternoon.

The police compound serves as a district-level police headquarters, housing key offices of the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD), Special Branch and several other police units.

“At least 31 people, including 16 police personnel, have been killed and more than 100 injured so far in the militant attack and suicide bombing,” the official said.

“Several militants are still holed up in the Special Branch section of the Kohat Police Complex,” the police official told AFP on condition of anonymity.

“An exchange of fire with them has been ongoing since late last night. Their exact number remains unclear,” the official added.

A statement from the Kohat district health officer late on Friday (September 18, 2026) said that more than 100 people had been injured, the vast majority of them police personnel, and several were in a critical condition.

Local militant group Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, a faction linked to Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) — the Pakistani Taliban — has claimed responsibility for the attack.

Rubble, blown-out walls

AFP images showed military personnel standing by piles of bricks, rubble and blown-out walls following the attack, with soldiers carrying assault rifles guarding the complex.

Several ambulances were seen lining a street near the police compound.

Pakistan has blamed the increase in attacks in KP and the southern border province of Balochistan on militancy emanating from Afghanistan, where the Taliban government denies Afghan involvement.

The accusations have sparked a bitter rift and armed conflict between the neighbouring countries, and Pakistan has carried out deadly airstrikes it says target militants on Afghan soil.

The Taliban government in Kabul and the United Nations said dozens of civilians were killed in the latest Pakistani strikes on eastern Afghanistan in June.

Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the attack on Friday (September 18, 2026) evening, expressing “deep sorrow and regret over the injury of several people as a result of the blast”.

He directed the “best medical assistance be provided to the injured” and called for a report into the attack.

President Asif Ali Zardari expressed “regret” over the casualties, sending his “best wishes for the speedy recovery of those injured in the blast”.

“The complete elimination of Fitna-al-Khawarij and terrorists operating with foreign backing is essential for national security,” he said, using another term for the TTP group.

World.title: Nandigram by-poll, a reset for Mamata and Congress ties
World.content:
A lot happened over the past two days on Thursday (September 17, 2026) and Friday (September 18) that is likely to have a long bearing in West Bengal politics.

In the last hours on Thursday (September 17), the Election Commission of India froze the grass and twin flowers symbol and the name of All India Trinamool Congress. The Commission allocated separate symbols and names to both the rival factions of Trinamool Congress — the Mamata Banerjee faction and the Ritabrata Banerjee group. Mamata Banerjee and her loyalists were given the symbol of a football player alongside the name — Mamata All India Trinamool Congress, while the Ritabrata Banerjee faction was given the envelope symbol with the name — Democratic Trinamool Congress.

Congress backs Mamata

Even before Mamata Banerjee had formally reacted to the freezing of her party’s name and symbol, Congress leaders came to her defence. Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi criticised the ECI, saying the issue is not just Mamata Banerjee’s fight.

“It’s the fight of every political party, every voter who wants free and fair elections,” Mr. Gandhi posted on social media. The Congress leader said that when an entire party can be stolen, it’s hardly surprising that the votes of millions of Indians can be stolen too.

Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal also condemned the ECI’s decision and demanded that the party’s original symbol be restored to the Mamata Banerjee-led faction.

A withdrawal and an arrest

On Friday (September 18), as the Mamata Banerjee-led faction grappled with the loss of the original party name and symbol, its candidate for the Nandigram Assembly bypoll, Sanchita Pradhan (Dey), withdrew her candidature. Photographs of the candidate meeting West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari also surfaced on social media. With the deadline for filing nominations over, Mamata Banerjee announced her faction’s support for the Congress candidate, Milan Pradhan, in Nandigram. She also extended support to the Congress candidate in the Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll in Assam.

However, within hours of Mamata Banerjee announcing support for Mr. Pradhan, the Congress candidate was arrested by the West Bengal Police in connection with an old case linked to the Nandigram land agitation. The arrest triggered strong reactions from both the Congress and the Trinamool Congress. Mamata Banerjee questioned the timing of the arrest, particularly after announcing support for the Congress candidate.

“The BJP’s politics of vendetta and atrocities show a clear pattern. With manipulation, with vote loot, with intimidation the Election Agency-BJP partnership is killing democracy every day,” the former Chief Minister wrote on social media.

Mr. Gandhi described the arrest as a political revenge and murder of democracy. “The BJP has no faith in fair elections—that’s why it wants to cling to power sometimes through vote theft, sometimes through stealing governments, and sometimes through stealing parties. They don’t want to contest elections; they want to end the electoral fight altogether. The Congress will neither fear nor bow down. We will fight — and we will win,” Mr. Gandhi posted on social media.

Mamata – Congress alliance

The Trinamool Congress has seemed to face an existential crisis after the BJP swept to power in the West Bengal Assembly elections — with the majority of its Lok Sabha MPs and MLAs deserting Mamata Banerjee.

There appears to be a vacuum in the Opposition space in the State. The emerging understanding between the Congress and Mamata Banerjee could reshape the Opposition’s strategy in West Bengal. Weeks earlier, Mamata Banerjee had proposed that the Congress support her faction’s candidate in Nandigram in return for her faction supporting the Congress candidate in Rejinagar.

The local Congress leadership has historically been sceptical of Mamata Banerjee, particularly over the period between 2011 and 2021, when the Trinamool Congress was in power and the Congress alleged that the party engineered defections and weakened its organisation in the State. The recent developments, however, have brought the two parties together, leaving the State Congress leadership to navigate its reservations alongside the changing political circumstances.

Almost 28 years ago, Mamata Banerjee broke away from the Congress to form the Trinamool Congress. Now, amid a crisis over her party’s identity and symbol, she is seeking Congress’s support.
